title: Spectrum Stampede
text:
Early game (turns 1 to 3)

Turn 1: Sazh’s Chocobo is the ideal opener — it grows with every land.
Turn 2: Bristly Bill, Sabotender or Bloom Tender. Bristly Bill spreads counters; Sabotender begins the drain clock; Bloom Tender is only worth it if you already have a red or green partner in hand.
Crack Evolving Wilds or Terramorphic Expanse only when you want the trigger or need the colour — they enter untapped and fetch a tapped basic, so they are never a wasted turn.
Do not overextend into a sweeper with a pure Bloom Tender board; its value is mana, not pressure.

title: Spectrum Stampede
text:
Mid game (turns 4 to 6)

Land Icetill Explorer or Prismatic Undercurrents as soon as possible. These are the two cards that turn the deck from a normal curve deck into a combo deck.
With Icetill Explorer, lands in the graveyard are playable: replay a spent Evolving Wilds, sacrifice it again, and fetch another basic. One card produces two landfall triggers every turn.
With Prismatic Undercurrents, an empty hand of lands is a feature — it fetches two basics to hand and then lets you play two lands a turn.
Use Explosive Prodigy as removal, not as a body: with a green and a red permanent in play it kills a two-toughness creature on entry for two mana.

title: Spectrum Stampede
text:
The combo turn
The deck’s big turn is a landfall storm, not an infinite loop:

Have Prismatic Undercurrents or Icetill Explorer in play (ideally both) plus two or more landfall payoffs (Sazh’s Chocobo, Bristly Bill, Tifa Lockhart, Mossborn Hydra, Rampaging Baloths, Sabotender, Tannuk, Memorial Ensign).
Play your land for turn (trigger one), a second land via the extra land drop (trigger two), and if Icetill Explorer is out, replay a fetch land from the graveyard and sacrifice it for a basic — two more triggers.
Each trigger fires independently on every payoff: Sabotender and Tannuk each deal 1 damage to the opponent, Mossborn Hydra doubles its counters, Rampaging Baloths makes a Beast, Tifa doubles her power.
Attack with the resulting board. Mossborn Hydra is usually lethal alone after two doublings; Tifa Lockhart doubles per trigger and tramples; the Beast and counter army follows.
Activate Rogue’s Passage on the largest attacker, and attack with Restless Ridgeline to give another attacker +2/+0 and untap it for a second hit.

title: Spectrum Stampede
text:
Win condition 2: the landfall drain
Sabotender and Tannuk, Memorial Ensign both read “whenever a land you control enters, this creature deals 1 damage to each opponent.” With two or three lands entering a turn, that is a steady 2 to 6 damage a turn that ignores combat entirely. Tannuk also draws a card on the second trigger each turn, so the drain engine refills your hand while it kills. This plan wins through board stalls, through blockers, and through decks that race better in combat — the land drops happen regardless.

title: Spectrum Stampede
text:
Mulligan guide

Keep: two or three lands with green and red available, plus an early landfall payoff (Sazh’s Chocobo, Bristly Bill, Sabotender) or Bloom Tender.
Keep (engine hands): a hand with Icetill Explorer or Prismatic Undercurrents plus four lands is a genuine keep even with no two-drop — the engine converts it.
Trim: hands with only six-drops, one-land hands, or hands whose only red source is a fetch land you must crack before casting anything.
The deck mulligans well because so many cards are interchangeable landfall payoffs; do not keep a hand for a single specific card.

title: Spectrum Stampede
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Vivid counts colours, not cards. Two green creatures and one red creature is a colour count of two, not three. Keep at least one red permanent alive if you are holding Explosive Prodigy, Squawkroaster or Prismabasher.
Squawkroaster’s power is a setting, not a base. It is always equal to your current colour count, so it swings for 2 with double strike in a clean Gruul board and shrinks if your board is wiped to a single colour.
Mossborn Hydra’s counters double, they do not add. Two landfall triggers in one turn take it from one counter to four; three take it to eight.
Prismatic Undercurrents searches, it does not put lands onto the battlefield. The lands go to hand and are played with your normal and extra land drops — so a full hand plus extra drops is the ideal state.
Icetill Explorer’s graveyard play is a land drop, not a spell. Replaying Evolving Wilds uses your land for the turn; if you have already played a land, use Prismatic Undercurrents or another extra-drop effect to keep going.
Tannuk draws only on the second resolution each turn. Sequence land drops so that at least two lands enter after Tannuk resolves, ideally with a fetch land cracking in between.
Restless Ridgeline enters tapped. Play it on a turn where you do not need the mana immediately, or fetch it off Fabled Passage and untap it with four lands out.
Bristly Bill’s activated ability doubles counters on every creature you control — it is the deck’s late-game finisher and combos directly with Sazh’s Chocobo and Mossborn Hydra piles.

title: Spectrum Stampede
text:
Matchups

Aggro: Sabotender and Rampaging Baloths provide reach blockers, and the drain plan races well because it does not need to attack. Explosive Prodigy is your cheapest interaction — hold it for the biggest threat.
Control: the lands-and-counters plan is resilient. Rebuild with a single Rampaging Baloths or Mossborn Hydra after a sweeper, and lean on Tannuk’s card draw. Rogue’s Passage makes the rebuilt threat unblockable the turn it lands.
Midrange: your top end outclasses theirs once Mossborn Hydra and Tifa Lockhart have doubled a few times. Trade early, then attack with a single enormous trampler.
Combo: you have no counterspells, so race. The drain plus a fast counter clock often wins before a slower combo assembles; Explosive Prodigy can remove a key combo creature.

title: Flicker Clock
text:
Early game
Open with a one-drop. Dream Beavers is the best of them because the drain is damage and the scry is a free look; Virulent Emissary is the better blocker and the better card once the board is wide. Turn two is Abuelo, Ancestral Echo if you have it, because a 2/2 flier that threatens a repeatable flicker changes how the opponent attacks. Do not spend Personify on a one-drop just to gain a card’s worth of value; hold it for a creature the opponent must answer.

title: Flicker Clock
section: Mid game and the combo turn
text:
Mid game and the combo turn
The first Overlord to impending is Overlord of the Hauntwoods, because the Everywhere land is the mana for everything afterwards. The second is whatever the hand supports: Floodpits if the hand is short on action, Mistmoors if you want the clock. Once an Overlord is on the battlefield, Personify and Abuelo are two-mana repeat triggers of its enters ability, which is why the deck plays eight cheap flicker effects around seven Overlords.
The actual kill is Bloodthirsty Conqueror plus Enduring Tenacity. With both on the battlefield, one life gained is one life drained, which is one life gained, with no player choice to break the chain: an opponent at any life total loses the game the moment a single drain or lifegain trigger resolves. Chain it from Dream Beavers entering, from Virulent Emissary watching any creature enter, from a Bat token, or from an Overlord’s Insects. Against opponents who can remove the pair, Another Round and the Overlords are the plan B, and Rogue’s Passage is how the plan B actually finishes.

title: Flicker Clock
text:

When the drain pair is answered or never arrives, the deck wins on the classic evasion axis. Overlord of the Mistmoors makes two 2/1 fliers per entry or attack, Another Round with X at two makes that three times over in one turn, and Sanguine Evangelist’s Bats and Kyoshi Warriors’ Allies add bodies to the count. Rogue’s Passage then removes the only relevant blocker, and Overlord of the Hauntwoods makes the extra lands so the passage and the Overlords can both be paid for. Note that Another Round also re-triggers Virulent Emissary’s lifegain once per pass, so a large Another Round can end the game through the drain loop instead of through damage.

title: Flicker Clock
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep two to four lands with at least two of the four colours showing and one creature that costs one or two. Keep any hand with Rogue’s Passage plus an Overlord, because those hands have a real clock. Pitch hands with only one colour of source and no Crystal Grotto, hands with Overlords but no early play, and hands with both copies of Enduring Tenacity and no Conqueror and no creatures.

title: Flicker Clock
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Impending means the Overlord is not a creature while time counters remain, so creature-only flickers (Personify, Abuelo, Another Round) cannot target it until the last counter comes off. Blink the small creatures instead; the Overlord still triggers once on entry, and the counters tick down every end step, including your opponent’s.
Overlord of the Hauntwoods makes a tapped land token, so it is mana for the following turn, not the current one. Plan the Everywhere land one turn ahead of the Overlord you want to cast with it.
Abuelo, Ancestral Echo returns the exiled creature at the beginning of the next end step, not immediately. It is a slow flicker with a fast body; use it on the opponent’s end step when you can, so the creature comes back before your own turn.
Enduring Tenacity returns as an enchantment when it dies, not as a creature, and it still drains. Do not let the opponent’s removal convince you the combo is gone.
Bloodthirsty Conqueror’s lifegain triggers on any life loss, including damage and combat, so the loop can start from a combat step rather than from a spell.
Another Round returns creatures under their owners’ control, so it also resets a creature an opponent has stolen.
Crystal Grotto and the fetch lands enter or cost mana to use, so an opening hand of Crystal Grotto plus two fetch lands is a slow hand even with three lands in it.

title: Fieldwork Syllabus
text:
Overview
This deck fuses two mechanics that feed each other. Explore is the fuel: every explore either puts a land into hand (fixing and landfall) or puts a +1/+1 counter on a body that is already cheap. Prepared is the payoff: prepared creatures let you cast a free copy of their spell, so cards that enter prepared are effectively two-for-ones, and Tam turns each landfall trigger into another free card.
The loop that matters is land-driven. Explore effects hand you lands, Nicanzil, Current Conductor puts those lands onto the battlefield tapped when a creature explores a land card, and each land that enters re-arms Tam, Observant Sequencer, which then casts a free Deep Sight to draw a card and gain a life. Studious First-Year does the same thing off the top: it enters prepared with Rampant Growth, so turn one is a 1/1 plus a free land onto the battlefield, which is a landfall trigger on turn one.
Nothing in the deck costs more than four mana, so the engine is online while the opponent is still setting up. The deck wins by turning explores into damage: Merfolk Cave-Diver gets +1/+0 and becomes unblockable for each explore trigger, and the deck can generate a lot of triggers in a single turn between Map tokens, Jadelight Spelunker, Over the Edge, and animated Restless lands.

title: Fieldwork Syllabus
text:
Approach

Game plan phases
Turns 1 to 2, establish the engine. Land a one-drop that either explores (Cenote Scout), makes a Map token (Spyglass Siren), or enters prepared with a free spell (Studious First-Year, Elite Interceptor). Turns 3 to 4, convert explores into pressure. Kinjalli’s Dawnrunner and Merfolk Cave-Diver are the two payoffs that turn a board of small explorers into a clock. Over the Edge on turn two or three explores twice on one creature, which is four points of Cave-Diver growth if both are nonland cards.

title: Fieldwork Syllabus
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Lead with Cenote Scout or Spyglass Siren. Scout’s explore is card selection plus a counter, and Siren’s Map token is a stored explore for later. Studious First-Year is the strongest turn one when you already hold a two-drop: the free Rampant Growth ramps you to three mana on turn two and triggers landfall.
Do not crack Map tokens early unless the explore does something. A Map is worth much more once Merfolk Cave-Diver or Nicanzil is on the battlefield, and Twists and Turns makes each one a scry plus an explore.


The combo turn
The explosive turn is Jadelight Spelunker for a large X, or Over the Edge on a creature that already has explore synergies. Sequence it like this:

Twists and Turns on the battlefield first if you have it, so every explore is scry 1 then explore.
Nicanzil down, so land-explores put lands from hand onto the battlefield tapped.
Cast Jadelight Spelunker with X = 4 or more. Each explore that hits a land pulls another land out of hand, which re-triggers Tam and any other landfall payoffs; each nonland explore puts a counter on the Spelunker.
Merfolk Cave-Diver grows by one power per trigger and becomes unblockable, so a five-trigger turn usually ends the game on the following attack.

Because Cave-Diver’s bonus is until end of turn, the damage has to happen in the same turn as the triggers. Attack after the explores, not before.


Win condition 2
When Cave-Diver is answered, the manabase finishes the game. Restless Anchorage becomes a 2/3 flier for {1}{W}{U} and makes a Map token whenever it attacks, so it grinds out damage and fuels Cave-Diver at the same time. Restless Vinestalk is a 5/5 trampler for {3}{G}{U} that also resets another attacker to base 3/3, which is a real upgrade on a 1/1 double striker or a 2/1 Painter.


Mulligan guide
Keep one-land hands only with a one-drop and a second land in the top three. Keep any hand with two lands plus a one-drop and a two-drop. Ship hands with no one-drop, because the deck’s whole plan is spending the first two turns building a board that makes explores matter. A hand of three lands, Nicanzil, and two explore creatures is a snap keep.


Key interactions and edge cases

Explore with a land on top puts the land into hand, not a counter. If the land is the only card you want, put the revealed nonland on the bottom only when the graveyard matters.
Nicanzil’s land ability is optional and triggers on the land being explored, not on any land entering. With Twists and Turns the explore still counts as exploring a land card.
Tam becomes prepared from landfall but only unprepares when you actually cast the Deep Sight copy. Multiple landfall triggers in one turn still only give you one Deep Sight unless you cast it in between.
Prepared copies are cast for free, so the Rampant Growth copy from Studious First-Year ramps without mana and triggers landfall on the same turn.
Harmonized Trio needs two untapped creatures to become prepared; Map tokens are artifacts, not creatures, so they cannot pay that cost.
Restless Vinestalk’s attack trigger sets base power and toughness, so +1/+1 counters from explore still apply on top of the 3/3.
Over the Edge’s destroy mode is the only main-deck answer to artifacts and enchantments. Do not fire it as a double explore if a Rest in Peace style effect is about to lock the graveyard plan.

Grind with Tam and Landscape Painter; the deck draws more cards than most midrange shells once landfall is online


Control
Do not overextend into sweepers. Hold one prepared creature and one Map token, then rebuild in a single turn with Jadelight Spelunker


Combo
Race. The deck goldfishes quickly, so use Over the Edge on their engine piece and keep Cave-Diver unblockable every turn

Morbid checks “a creature died this turn” — any creature, including your opponent’s. Trades and their removal feed Pack, Prowler and Wardens for free.

The Misty Mountains Cold resolves fully into a 6/6 flying Dragon; Magda converts three Treasures into haste Dragons on demand; Smaug, Wicked Worm is a 5/5 flyer that can enter with a Treasure per opposing artifact; Rapacious Dragon brings two Treasures and a 3/3 flyer. title: Scale and Coin
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two or three lands and a two-drop engine (Magda, Sarkhan, Sackville-Bagginses, Collector’s Vault). Hands with Smaug the Magnificent plus any Treasure source are strong. Ship one-landers, hands with three or more five-drops, and hands with no red source. Against aggressive decks, prioritize Gleaming Barrier and Nowhere to Run over the slow draw pieces; against control, keep Spell Pierce and lean on Cavern of Souls naming Dragon.

title: Scale and Coin
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Smaug’s attack trigger deals damage equal to your Treasure count at the moment the trigger resolves — sacrifice Treasures for mana after declaring attackers, not before, if you want maximum damage.
Fateful Discovery triggers on artifacts entering, not tokens specifically: Treasure tokens, Gleaming Barrier, Collector’s Vault, and Cavern-free artifact creatures all draw. The Misty Mountains Cold’s four chapter triggers each draw a card with Fateful Discovery out.
The Misty Mountains Cold checks for four or more Treasures after each chapter trigger, then sacrifices itself for a 6/6 Dragon — it needs four Treasures, not four counters, so time your Treasure spends carefully if you want the Dragon rather than the mana.
Magda’s Treasure trigger fires once per turn regardless of how many crimes you commit — one crime per turn is enough.
“Commit a crime” means targeting the opponent, anything they control, or cards in their graveyard — Nowhere to Run, removal, and even a counterspell aimed at their spell are crimes.
Desolation of Smaug damages non-Dragon creatures — your Dragon tokens and Dragons survive while everything else on both sides takes 3. The four mana it adds can only cast Dragon spells.
The Sackville-Bagginses’ token-sacrifice ping includes Treasure tokens sacrificed for mana — cracking a Treasure at the right moment doubles as a Shock.
Cavern of Souls must name Dragon before it taps for the uncounterable any-color mana; it only protects Dragon creature spells.
Wicked Worm draws when you cast a spell with mana from a Treasure — mana from Cavern, basic lands or treasures all mix, so this triggers only if Treasure mana was actually spent on that spell.

Midrange (landfall, counters): the Treasure-draw engine out-values them — every Treasure replaces itself and every Dragon is bigger than their curve; Desolation clears their developed board and ramps into a Dragon on the same turn.
Control: Cavern of Souls (naming Dragon), Spell Pierce and Wicked Worm’s treasure-cast draw keep gas flowing; the saga and enchantment engines (Misty Mountains Cold, Fateful Discovery, Last Light of Durin’s Day) are hard for sweepers to answer permanently.
Combo and big mana: the deck is the aggressor — haste Smaug and Magda Dragons pressure before their engine comes online, and Nowhere to Run plus Spell Pierce disrupt key pieces.

title: Everything Must Go
text:
Overview
Nothing in this deck is meant to stay on the battlefield. Every permanent is fuel, and the deck wins by converting that fuel into life loss for the opponent.
The engine has three layers:

Fuel. Market Gnome, Piggy Bank, Vinereap Mentor and Tolls of War all leave something behind when they die. Dying is not a cost here, it is the plan.
Outlets. Popular Egotist, Cauldron of Essence and Fountainport let you kill your own permanents on demand, every turn, without spending cards to do it.
Payoffs. Vengeful Bloodwitch, Cauldron of Essence, Wispdrinker Vampire, Bloodletter of Aclazotz and Vein Ripper each turn a death into an opponent losing life while you gain it.

The combo finish comes from the two vampires at the top of the curve. Bloodthirsty Conqueror gives you back every point an opponent loses, and Enduring Tenacity turns every point you gain back into a point an opponent loses. Put both on the battlefield and any single point of opponent life loss, from a dying creature, a sacrifice to Popular Egotist, the start of combat with Sinister Monolith, or a Fountainport activation, becomes an endless loop of life loss. Three copies of each piece plus nine separate drain triggers means the deck finds the loop in most games it survives to turn five.
Sinister Monolith is the quiet all-star: it drains at the beginning of every combat on your turn for free, which is exactly the spark the loop needs, and it can be cashed in later for two cards.

title: Everything Must Go
text:
Approach

Game plan
Turns 1 to 2, build the fuel line. Deploy Market Gnome or Piggy Bank, ideally both. These are the cards opponents least want to spend removal on, and they replace themselves the moment an outlet eats them. Vengeful Bloodwitch is the best two-drop in the deck: it is simultaneously an outlet target, a drain payoff, and the trigger that starts the combo.
Turns 3 to 4, add the machinery. Land an outlet (Popular Egotist, Cauldron of Essence) and a drain body. Start sacrificing on every end step. Tolls of War converts each sacrifice into a 1/1 Ally, and Gleaming Geardrake grows a counter every time an artifact, Treasure, Clue or Food hits the graveyard. Sinister Monolith can come down here as a free engine that drains without any input.
Turn 5 and later, close. A single Bloodthirsty Conqueror plus a single Enduring Tenacity plus any drain trigger ends the game on the spot. If the loop is not assembled, the deck still wins through a swarm of Fish, Ally, Food and Treasure tokens that get sacrificed for cards and pushed through with the Restless Cottage manland.

title: Everything Must Go
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Lead with fuel that pays you back. Market Gnome is the ideal turn one: a 0/3 that draws a card and gains a life when it dies is a card that trades up against any removal spell. Piggy Bank ramps you toward the four and five mana combo pieces. Against an opponent with a fast start, hold Get Lost rather than tapping out for a sacrificial body.
Do not attack with the fodder. These creatures are worth more dead than alive, and every point of damage they deal is incidental.


Mid game
The turn you deploy an outlet, the deck stops being a pile of small creatures and starts being an engine. Popular Egotist is the cleanest: pay one black and sacrifice a permanent each turn, and every sacrifice drains the opponent for one and gains you one, which also makes Bloodthirsty Conqueror gain life on its own.
Wispdrinker Vampire is the other key midgame card. Every creature token with power two or less that enters under your control (the 1/1 Ally tokens from Tolls of War and the 1/1 Fish from Fountainport both qualify) makes each opponent lose one life and gains you one. Since the deck produces creature tokens on every sacrifice, Wispdrinker turns the trickle into a stream, and any one of those triggers is enough to ignite the loop once the two combo pieces are down.


The combo turn
Assemble Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Enduring Tenacity, then make the opponent lose one life. The order matters only for the first trigger:

Opponent loses 1 life to any drain effect.
Bloodthirsty Conqueror gains you that 1 life.
Enduring Tenacity makes a target opponent lose 1 life.
Back to step 2, forever.

Bloodthirsty Conqueror is also a 5/5 flying deathtouch body, so it wins games the slow way when the loop is not online, and Enduring Tenacity is a 4/3 that returns to the battlefield as a non-creature enchantment when it dies, which makes it very difficult to answer permanently with creature removal.


Win condition 2
Without both combo pieces, the deck goes wide and finishes with tiny creatures. Tolls of War turns each sacrifice into an Ally, Fountainport manufactures Fish and Treasures, Vinereap Mentor and Restless Cottage produce Food, and Gleaming Geardrake grows into a real flying threat off every artifact sacrificed. Add the non-infinite drain from Vengeful Bloodwitch, Cauldron of Essence, Wispdrinker Vampire and a single Bloodletter of Aclazotz, which doubles every point of life the opponent loses on your turn, and the swarm only needs to connect once or twice.


Mulligan guide
Keep hands with two or three lands, at least one two-drop, and at least one card that drains or sacrifices. Six-card keeps are fine if they contain Vengeful Bloodwitch plus a land-heavy start.
Send back hands with no black source, hands with four or more lands and no engine, and hands that are all combo pieces and no fodder. A hand of Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Enduring Tenacity, Vein Ripper and four lands looks powerful and does nothing until turn five.


Key interactions and edge cases

Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles opponent life loss on your turn only. With Bloodthirsty Conqueror out, each point of drain becomes two life gained, and with Enduring Tenacity it accelerates the loop rather than being required for it.
Cauldron of Essence does double duty: every creature that dies drains the table, and its activation sacrifices a creature to return a creature card from your graveyard for {1}{B}{G}. Recycling a Vinereap Mentor or Market Gnome re-arms the engine.
Enduring Tenacity returns as an enchantment, which matters twice. Creature removal will not keep it dead, and it can later be fed to Popular Egotist, which accepts creatures or enchantments.
Fountainport needs a token to sacrifice. Play Treasures and Fish before you need cards; keep one spare token in reserve so the draw is always available.
Popular Egotist only sacrifices permanents you control that are creatures or enchantments, so Treasures and Clues are not legal fuel for it. Use Cauldron of Essence and the outlets on creature tokens instead.
Vein Ripper drains two per creature death, which is a full loop’s worth of triggers with a single sacrifice, and its ward, sacrifice a creature, makes it painful to remove.
Sinister Monolith drains at the beginning of combat on your turn with no input from you. If the opponent is at a low life total, do not forget it can be cashed in for two cards at instant speed during the end step.



Matchups
Against aggro. You have more life gain than most decks can punch through. Trade fodder for time, use Get Lost on the biggest threat, and let Cauldron of Essence and Vengeful Bloodwitch undo their work. If the loop appears before turn six, racing stops mattering.
Against control. Do not overextend into a sweeper; the deck’s creatures are meant to be sacrificed, not kept. Force them to answer Bloodthirsty Conqueror on sight, then rebuild with Enduring Tenacity, which survives creature removal.
Against midrange. This is the deck’s best matchup. Your creatures die for value, so their removal always leaves you with a token, a Food or a card.
Against graveyard decks. Restless Cottage exiles a card every time it attacks, and sacrifice outlets let you choose what never reaches the graveyard. Fountainport and Cauldron of Essence give you more relevant actions per turn than most recursion decks.

Interaction
Ruling detail




Amass and the Army token
The first amass in a game creates the 0/0 black Goblin Army token and then puts the counters on it. Every later amass just adds counters to that same Army, so the deck only ever has one Army unless it dies


The Great Goblin counts events, not counters
Its trigger reads “one or more counters”, so amass 4 is a single trigger and a single 2 damage. Two separate amass 1 spells are two triggers and 4 damage. Cheap spells are worth more than large ones with this card on the board


The Great Goblin’s second ability
Whenever another Goblin, Orc, or Army you control dies, you exile the top card of your library and may play it until the end of your next turn. Fearsome Goblin Pair dying triggers both abilities: amass 4 first, then the exile


Azog gives counters to whoever owned the creature
Azog destroys another creature and its controller amasses counters equal to that creature’s power. Killing an opposing 1/1 hands them a single counter. If you control the destroyed creature, you amass and draw a card


Wargling needs power four
Ferocious checks for any creature you control with power four or greater when Wargling attacks. Misty Mountains Raider (4/4) and an Army with four or more counters both qualify


Warg Tactics is an instant
The counter, trample and hexproof mode can be cast in response to removal, during combat, or on the opponent’s turn. The flying mode is the deck’s only clean answer to fliers


Goblin-town is sorcery speed and one-shot
The sacrifice ability can only be activated as a sorcery, and the land is gone afterwards. Activate it in the second main phase after the Army has attacked


Tidings of War flashback
The flashback cast is a spell cast from the graveyard, so it counts as a noncreature spell for Bothersome Noisemaker and gives the Army another counter on top of the amass 3


Hybrid costs
The Great Goblin, Fearsome Goblin Pair and Goblin Plate Mail can each be paid with black or red mana, so the deck rarely gets stuck on a colour

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
Curve and mana
Twenty-seven lands: six fetches, sixteen nonbasic duals and utility lands, and four basics (one of each color). The mana base is built to hit green or black on turn one or two, blue and red by turn three, and to keep a fetch uncracked when a Disappear trigger is needed later.
The nonland curve is 33 cards with an average mana value of about 3.0: five one-drops (the Spree instants and Insatiable Avarice), fourteen two-drops (Bloom Tender, Explosive Prodigy, Rat King, Candy Grapple, Lively Dirge), six four-drops (Squawkroaster, Lord Dregg), six five-drops (Pizza Face, Shimmercreep, Glister Bairn) and two six-drops (Krang and Shredder). The deck reaches four lands on turn four roughly three games out of four, and the goldfish tests show a consistent turn-four board.

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
Early game
Lead with a two-drop that puts a color on the board: Bloom Tender (green), Explosive Prodigy (red, and it removes a creature on entry), or Rat King, Verminister (black). Hold fetch lands. A hand of fetch plus Rat King is the dream opener: turn two Rat King, turn three crack the fetch for a basic, and the Rat King’s Disappear trigger makes a Rat and grows itself at your end step. Phantom Interference and Metamorphic Blast are fine turn-one plays against aggressive decks only when needed; mostly you want them saved as answers.

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
Mid game
Land Lord Dregg, Insect Invader or Pizza Face on four mana. Lord Dregg turns every triggered end step into a flying token and every spare token into a card. Pizza Face creates the Food token that keeps your colored permanents safe as bargain fodder. Squawkroaster wants to come down when at least three colors are on board so it attacks as a 3-power double striker immediately. Do not sacrifice colored permanents casually: the Vivid count is the deck’s mana and its damage, so sacrifice colorless tokens, Foods, and fetch lands first.

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
The combo turn
The signature sequence starts with a fetch in play and a Disappear card on the battlefield. Crack the fetch at instant speed during combat or in the opponent’s turn. At the beginning of your end step every Disappear ability sees a permanent left this turn and fires: Rat King makes a Rat and grows, Lord Dregg makes an Insect, Pizza Face puts three counters on your biggest creature. Then cash the tokens in: sacrifice a token to Lord Dregg to draw, or bank three Rats for Rat King’s reanimation later. With Krang and Shredder, attack first to exile cards from the top of the opponent’s library, then the same end step casts one of them for free. The kill turn: Bloom Tender taps for four or five mana, Glister Bairn pumps the Squawkroaster at the start of combat, and Rogue’s Passage makes it unblockable; a 4-color Squawkroaster hits for 8, a 5-color one for 10, and with Glister Bairn’s X pump the swing ends the game.

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
Win condition 2
The Shimmercreep drain loop. Each Shimmercreep entry deals X damage to the opponent and gains X life, where X is the color count, so a single 5-color entry is a 10-life swing. The deck recurs it: Rat King sacrifices three Rats to return a creature from the graveyard (Shimmercreep included), Lively Dirge returns engine pieces up to total mana value 4, and Krang and Shredder keeps the board and hand stocked by casting the opponent’s own cards. The drain, plus Food lifegain and Pizza Face’s 15-life activation, outlasts anything that cannot kill in one turn.

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two or three lands and at least one two-drop creature in the deck’s early colors (green, black, or red). A fetch land plus Rat King, Verminister or Lord Dregg is a strong engine start. Ship one-lander openers, hands without colored sources for the first two spells, and hands of nothing but five-drops and six-drops. Against aggro, favor early removal (Explosive Prodigy, Candy Grapple) and lifegain pieces; against control, keep the Spree counterspells and a fast Squawkroaster clock.

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Disappear checks the whole turn, not just your actions: a fetch crack, a bargain sacrifice, or a blocker dying all arm the end-step triggers.
The Vivid count is colors among permanents you control, so tokens matter: Phantom Interference’s white Spirit adds a fifth color even though the deck is GUBR, and colored tokens (Rats, Insects) add black.
Squawkroaster’s power is set by the count each time it is checked; it shrinks if you sacrifice your only red or green permanent, so keep one of each color when possible.
Bloom Tender produces one mana per color present, up to five, but it must tap after your colors are on board, so sequence spells before activating it.
Lord Dregg’s draw requires sacrificing a token, which itself arms Disappear for the same end step, creating a small loop.
Rat King’s reanimation needs exactly three Rats; Lord Dregg’s Insects do not count, so save Rats when planning to reanimate Shimmercreep.
Krang and Shredder exiles from each opponent and you may cast one card exiled with it per Disappear end step, for free.
Restless Vinestalk’s attack trigger sets another creature’s base power and toughness to 3/3, which would erase Squawkroaster’s color-count power, so never target it.
Rogue’s Passage’s activation is sorcery-speed only in the sense that it must be used before attackers are declared; activate it in the first main phase.
Metamorphic Blast’s Rabbit mode is tempo: it shrinks an attacker or blocker to 0/1 until end of turn, buying a full turn against a large threat.

title: Prismatic Departure
text:
Matchups

Aggro (fliers, lifegain, cats): Explosive Prodigy and Candy Grapple clear early threats, Lord Dregg’s flying Insects block, and Food lifegain plus Shimmercreep’s gain stabilize before the drain finishes the race.
Midrange (counters, landfall): the recursion engine out-values one-for-one removal; every Rat and Insect is a card through Lord Dregg, and Krang and Shredder mills their best topdecks.
Control: Spree counterspells protect the engine, Disappear triggers rebuild the board after sweepers, and the tutor suite (Insatiable Avarice, Lively Dirge) finds the answer.
Combo and big mana: the deck is the aggressor, clocking with a double-striking Squawkroaster through Rogue’s Passage before their engine comes online.

Early game
Turns one and two should establish two of the three mechanics at once. Starfighter Pilot is the best opener against removal-light decks: a 2/2 that surveils every time it pays a waterbend cost, and with Matoya, Archon Elder that becomes a repeatable draw. Water Tribe Rallier is the waterbend outlet you can cast on turn two and then never pay for again: five untapped creatures and artifacts cover waterbend five entirely, so look at four cards and take the creature for free. title: Tidewater Tally

Katara, Bending Prodigy is the counter clock. She taps for any waterbend cost, including her own waterbend six draw, and the end step checks whether she is tapped, so the deck is rewarded for spending her as currency every single turn. Terrasymbiosis converts the first counter event of each turn into cards: Earth King’s Lieutenant handing out counters, Araña’s attack trigger, United Front, or the counter Katara puts on herself all draw.
Waterbender Ascension is the engine that scales fastest. Any creature connecting adds a quest counter, and at four or more it draws a card on every subsequent trigger, so a wide board of small attackers turns it into a steady stream of cards. Its second ability is the deck’s removal-proof answer: waterbend four makes a creature unblockable, and if the board is wide enough, four tapped creatures is no cost at all.
Surveil keeps the draws clean. Twilight Diviner surveils two on entry, Broodspinner surveils two and later sacrifices into a swarm of flying Insects equal to the card types in your graveyard, and every surveil land is a free look. Matoya, Archon Elder turns each of them into a card, so playing lands off the top of the library is how this deck keeps hitting its fourth and fifth land without flooding.

title: Tidewater Tally

The combo turn

Count your currency. Untapped artifacts and creatures, no matter how small, how recently played or how badly they attack, each pay one generic mana of a waterbend cost.

Or set the team. Katara, Water Tribe’s Hope’s waterbend X makes every creature you control base X/X until end of turn, and X cannot be zero. Make the biggest one unblockable for waterbend four, pump it with Secluded Starforge, and the deck’s wide cheap board is the payment. Broodspinner’s sacrifice is the grindy backup: flying Insect tokens equal to the card types in your graveyard is a real clock in a deck that surveils this much.

Keep two to three lands and at least one two-drop that touches two mechanics: Starfighter Pilot or Water Tribe Rallier first, Rocketeer Boostbuggy or Earth King’s Lieutenant second. title: Tidewater Tally
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Waterbend is not a tap ability. “For each generic mana in that cost, you may tap an untapped artifact or creature you control rather than pay that mana,” and the ruling is explicit that you may tap a creature you have not controlled since the start of your turn. Summoning-sick creatures, spare Vehicles, Treasures and Robot tokens all pay, so board width matters more than size.
If an artifact or creature has a mana ability with tap in the cost, activating that ability while paying a waterbend cost taps it first, and you cannot tap it again for waterbend. Do not plan a land-fetch or mana creature as your waterbend payment in the same window.
Katara, Water Tribe’s Hope sets base power and toughness, which overwrites counters and pumps for the turn rather than adding to them, and it can only be activated during your turn with X of at least one. Pay it with artifacts and creatures you are not attacking with, because paying for it taps the payment.
Waterbender Ascension draws on every trigger once it has four or more quest counters, not just the fourth one, so a wide attack with several connecting creatures can draw multiple cards in a single combat.
Crashing Wave’s X is the amount of generic mana you actually waterbend, and you tap up to X target creatures before distributing three stun counters among any tapped creatures your opponents control, including creatures that were already tapped. If every target becomes illegal before it resolves, the spell does not resolve and no stun counters are distributed.
Loading Zone doubles counters for every creature you control. With Terrasymbiosis, the doubled number is what the draw effect sees on that turn’s first counter event, so a single counter from Earth King’s Lieutenant becomes two counters and two cards.
Terrasymbiosis triggers only once each turn, on the first event that puts counters on a creature. United Front’s mass counter placement counts as several events but only the first one draws.
Earth King’s Lieutenant counts Allies: Water Tribe Rallier, Katara, Bending Prodigy, Flexible Waterbender, Foggy Swamp Vinebender, Katara, Water Tribe’s Hope, the Ally token she makes and every Ally token from United Front all trigger it.
Broodspinner’s Insects count card types among cards in your graveyard, and surveil lands put cards there for free, so the swarm is usually three to five tokens by the time it is sacrificed.
Twilight Diviner’s copy clause needs a creature that entered or was cast from a graveyard, which this build does not produce. Treat it as a 3/3 with surveil two and ignore the rest of the text.
Secluded Starforge’s pump is sorcery speed only and it taps the artifacts as part of the cost, so use it before combat and use artifacts, not creatures you want to attack with.

title: Dragon’s Ledger
text:

Keep any hand with a two-drop engine or Last Light plus three lands. Hands with Smaug the Magnificent and no Treasure source are too slow — the first ping needs a Treasure count. title: Dragon’s Ledger
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Smaug’s attack trigger hits any target — planeswalkers, players, or creatures — and resolves on each combat, so the extra combat from Desert Were-Worm means two triggers per turn.
Smaug, Wicked Worm draws only when mana from a Treasure pays for the spell; sacrifice Treasures on the cast, not before.
Last Light of Durin’s Day checks Mountain ETB, and its own Mountaincycling plus Troop of Ponies count. It sacrifices itself at six quest counters and tutors (hand and/or library) — with six Mountains and a Dragon in hand it simply puts it onto the battlefield.
Desert Were-Worm’s extra combat triggers only the first time each turn you attack with 12+ total power; it untaps all attackers, so Smaug, the Worm and the Dwarf tokens all swing twice.
The Lonely Mountain enters tapped unless you control an Equipment — one Equipment on board keeps all four copies untapped.
Desolation of Smaug’s four mana is Dragon-only; use it for Wicked Worm or Great Calamity, never for Gnashing of Teeth.
Through the Forest Gate can put any number of lands from the top twenty into play — with several Mountains that is multiple Last Light quest counters and a big Were-Worm in a single spell.

Control: sagas are sticky, Treasure mana makes it easy to hold up interaction, and Desolation punishes creature-light boards. Last Light’s tutor forces answers.
Combo race: the extra-combat turn ends the game faster than most opposing engines; Rogue’s Passage ignores chump blockers.

title: Web Slingback
text:
Early game (turns 1-3)

Turn 1: Aunt May or Llanowar Elves. Aunt May is the preferred engine start (every later Spider gains a counter); the Elf is the preferred sling toll (it has already made mana).
Turn 2: Mary Jane Watson first so Spider entries draw, then a second dork or Spider. Twitching Doll taps for any color and leaves a nest counter each time, so it both ramps and pays for itself later.
Turn 3: Spider-Man, Web-Slinger or Get Lost. Do not bounce the dork on the turn you need its mana; sling only when the creature being returned has already done its job.

title: Web Slingback
text:
Mid game (turns 4-6)

Attack with whatever the board has: attackers come back tapped, which is exactly the condition web-slinging needs.
Second main phase: cast Silk, Web Weaver or Spider-UK by returning a tapped attacker. If Silk is already out, every creature spell in the chain makes a Citizen; if Mary Jane is out, the entering Spider draws; Aunt May grows it.
Order the cast triggers for value: Mary Jane draws once per turn, so make the first Spider enter before casting the rest of the chain.
Spider-Man, Brooklyn Visionary smooths lands on entry; Web-Warriors turns a wide board into a big one in a single cast.

title: Web Slingback
text:

Attack with four or more creatures; keep one dork back untapped if you need its mana for the chain.
In the second main phase, return tapped attackers one at a time: each web-slinging cast is cheaper than the spell’s normal cost, so three casts cost about five mana total.
Each cast makes a Citizen (Silk), draws (Mary Jane, once), gains life and a counter on the entering Spider (Aunt May) and grows a creature (India).
Cast Wall Crawl or Web-Warriors if available, then activate Silk’s {3}{G}{W}: the team gets +2/+2 and vigilance.
Animate Restless Prairie and attack: the Llama adds +1/+1 to everything as it swings. With a half-dozen creatures this is lethal.

title: Web Slingback
text:
Win condition 2: the double-strike Spider
Origin of Spider-Man is a two-mana saga that builds its own finisher. Chapter I makes a 2/1 Spider token, chapter II puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature and turns it into a legendary Spider Hero (which keeps it inside every Spider payoff, including Mary Jane and Aunt May), and chapter III grants double strike. Point it at a Spider that Aunt May and India have been growing, or at a Web-Warriors-pumped 5/5, and the single unblocked hit is 10+ damage. Overprotect adds trample, hexproof and indestructible to make the swing unstoppable.

title: Web Slingback
text:
Mulligan guide

Keep: two to four lands with at least one white and one green source, a one- or two-drop engine (Aunt May, Mary Jane, Elf, Web-Slinger), and preferably one Spider to start the loop.
Trim: hands with five or more lands, all-toll hands with no actual web-slingers, and single-color hands that cannot cast both an engine and a Spider by turn 3.
Restless Prairie and Gathering Place enter tapped or conditionally, so count them as slow mana when judging a two-land hand.

title: Web Slingback
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

The returned creature must be tapped as you cast the spell; a creature that attacked this turn qualifies, and so does a dork you tapped for mana. Vigilance is not a problem because the deck grants it only through Silk’s overrun, on the turn you are attacking with it.
Web-slinging is an alternative cost, not a reduction: you pay the sling cost plus any additional costs, and you cannot combine it with other alternative costs.
Mary Jane Watson triggers once per turn no matter how many Spiders enter, so time the first Spider of your chain before the flood of casts.
Silk’s Citizen tokens are Humans, not Spiders, so they do not draw with Mary Jane or grow with Aunt May, but they do feed Wall Crawl, Web-Warriors, Silk’s overrun and Three Tree City only if you choose Spider for the city (it counts Spiders).
Aunt May’s counter trigger puts the counter on the Spider that entered; Spider-UK’s end-step draw needs two enters in the turn, which a standard chain exceeds.
Get Lost gives the opponent two Map tokens; use it on their engine rather than their small creatures to avoid the ramp.

title: Web Slingback

Aggro (fliers, lifegain, cat, landfall): Aunt May and Silk outsize their early creatures; Twitching Doll and Spiders-Man chump or block with reach; Get Lost answers their key threat and the deck’s lifegain (Aunt May, Spider-UK) buys the extra turn to overrun.
Midrange: win the board race with Web-Warriors and Wall Crawl; the recast chain out-values one-for-one removal because every bounced creature is replayed with a discount.
Control: hold Get Lost for their planeswalker, deploy Silk and India together so a single cast turn rebuilds the board after a sweeper, and lean on the Origin double-strike line to close before they stabilize.

The land half of the win condition. Two mana and a tap makes a creature that attacked this turn prepared, and four mana prepares any creature at all. With a re-preparer already running, this is a second free spell in the same turn, and with Draconic Visitor down that free spell is another Dragon


Rockfall Vale
Red-green dual that enters untapped from turn three onward, covering both halves of the Soul Tether cost


Haunted Ridge
Black-red dual on the same untap condition, paying for Void Extrapolator, Paradox Shaper and the black half of Stingerquill Voxmancer


Forest, Mountain, Swamp
Seven Forests carry the green half of the deck, four Mountains pay for Draconic Visitor and Aerid Konstrari, three Swamps cover the black splash

title: Rehearsed Ruin
text:
Curve and mana
36 creatures and 24 lands, average nonland mana value 2.36 — the curve is 9 ones, 15 twos, 6 threes, 2 fours and 4 fives, so there is a play on turn one and turn two in nearly every game. Nothing costs more than five.
Twenty of the thirty-six creatures are one or two mana, which matters because the deck wants to reach turn three with a prepared body and a re-preparer on the battlefield, not with a hand it cannot empty. The four five-drops are the only real top end: three Draconic Visitor and one Hungering Puppetbeast.
The mana base is green-red with a black splash. Green sources number fifteen and red twelve, which comfortably covers {G}, {R} and the {R/G} hybrid symbols on the Soul Tether cycle; the seven black sources exist for Void Extrapolator and Paradox Shaper, both of which are also castable through their hybrid {U/B} symbol if a black source is missing. Rockfall Vale and Haunted Ridge both enter untapped once you control two other lands, so the deck rarely loses a turn to its own duals. Hexhaven Dueling Arena produces only colourless mana, which is a real cost — treat it as the fourth land you play, not the second.

title: Rehearsed Ruin
text:
Early game (turns 1 to 3)

Turn 1: Heartwood Crafter is the best play — it enters prepared, so you can immediately cast the free Soul Tether for a Heartwood token, or hold the free spell until you need it. Pompous Battlemage is the second-best one-drop, and its free Improvised Act loots away a spare land.
Turn 2: Konstrari Improviser or Carnivorous Cultivator. Both arrive prepared. If you already have a Heartwood token, cast the free Soul Tether again — two Heartwoods is real mana.
Turn 3: Land a re-preparer (Woodwork Prodigy, Paradox Shaper, Stingerquill Voxmancer). From this point forward, each of your upkeeps starts with a free spell whether you do anything or not.
Do not attack into bigger blockers with Carnivorous Cultivator unless you need the land recursion — a 2/3 deathtouch that survives is worth more than two damage.

title: Rehearsed Ruin
text:
Mid game (turns 4 to 6)

Cast the free spells in the right order: Soul Tether first (tokens and mana), then Omit Variables (mills toward threshold and Tarmogoyf), then whatever is left over.
Draconic Visitor is the turn the deck turns the corner. Cast it only with a re-preparer already running or a prepared creature in hand; a 5/5 flier with no token stream behind it is just a fair Dragon.
Pia, Determined Rebuilder does two jobs at once. The Thopter it makes is an artifact that counts for its own pump ability, and the ability’s cost ({5} and one red) is exactly the kind of spare mana four Heartwoods provide.
Codie, Ravenous Codex is worth a turn when you have two or more prepared creatures. Every Soul Tether becomes two Heartwoods, and with a Draconic Visitor on the battlefield that is two Dragons.

title: Rehearsed Ruin
text:
The combo turn

Untap with a re-preparer (Woodwork Prodigy, Paradox Shaper or Stingerquill Voxmancer) on the battlefield, or a prepared body plus two spare mana for Hexhaven Dueling Arena.
Upkeep: the creature becomes prepared. Cast the copy of its spell — Soul Tether for a Heartwood token, doubled to two if Codie, Ravenous Codex is out.
If Draconic Visitor is on the battlefield, those Heartwood tokens arrive as 5/5 red Dragons with flying instead. Each one is a fresh attacker; three of them is a lethal swing in two turns.
With the mana the Heartwoods produced (they tap for red or green), activate Hexhaven Dueling Arena on a creature that attacked to prepare a second body, and cast that free spell too. Pia, Determined Rebuilder’s pump ability costs five mana and one red — Heartwood tokens are what pays for it.
Repeat on the next upkeep. Nothing here consumes a card: the creatures stay, the tokens stay, and the free spell comes back every turn.

title: Rehearsed Ruin
section: Win condition 2: attack with the whole board
text:
Win condition 2: attack with the whole board
The Heartwood and Thopter tokens are not just mana. Pia, Determined Rebuilder gives a target creature +X/+0 where X is the number of artifacts you control, and Aerid Konstrari does the same for itself with {6} — on a board with six or seven artifacts that is a 12-power attack out of a 2/2 and a 5/4. Hungering Puppetbeast converts spare artifacts into +1/+1 counters and either trample, hexproof or haste, and Tarmogoyf is usually a 3/4 or 4/5 for two mana by the time the self-mill has done its work. This is the plan when the opponent has an answer to the Dragons (a sweeper, a big flier, or a planeswalker that keeps making blockers).

title: Rehearsed Ruin
text:
Mulligan guide

Keep: two or three lands including a green source, plus one prepared one-drop or two-drop and one re-preparer. That is a functional hand — the deck needs a body and a way to re-prepare it, nothing more.
Keep on six: any hand with Heartwood Crafter plus two lands. One mana for a free Heartwood token is enough of a start.
Trim: one-land hands; hands with no green source; hands of Draconic Visitor plus lands with no token stream; four-land hands with no creature.
Because fifteen of the thirty-six nonland cards cost two, most six-card hands are playable. Do not go to five chasing a perfect curve.

title: Rehearsed Ruin
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Prepared is a state, not a trigger to spend. A creature that enters prepared has one free spell available whenever you want it. Casting the copy unprepares it — with a re-preparer, the state comes back at the next upkeep, which is the entire engine.
Draconic Visitor replaces tokens, it does not copy them. “If one or more artifact tokens would be created under your control, that many 5/5 red Dragon creature tokens with flying are created instead” — so the Heartwood token never exists, and you lose the mana rock but gain a Dragon. Only cast it once you have already banked the mana you need.
Draconic Visitor also affects the Thopter from Pia, Determined Rebuilder. A Thopter that becomes a 5/5 Dragon is a strict upgrade, and Pia’s pump ability still counts artifacts, so keep at least one non-token artifact on the battlefield if you want her ability to stay large.
Heartwood Crafter’s own mana is restricted. Its “{T}: Add {C}. This mana can’t be spent to cast spells from your hand” pays for Hexhaven Dueling Arena activations and other abilities, not for the next creature.
Codie, Ravenous Codex copies prepared spells only. The five-colour activation on its second ability needs all five colours and is not realistically usable in a three-colour deck — it is a bonus, not a plan.
Paradox Shaper can recycle. Its {2} ability puts a card from your graveyard on the bottom of your library, which matters once Tarmogoyf and threshold are online: do not let it shrink the yard you are counting on without a reason.
Carnivorous Cultivator plus Enroot is a land loop. The free Enroot puts a land into your graveyard; combat damage then returns a land card from the graveyard to your hand, so a chump-blocked Cultivator still returns a land you sacrificed nothing for.
Void Extrapolator and Theorix Metamage-style threshold cards want seven cards. Between Omit Variables (mill three, twice a turn with two copies of the effect) and the free soul-tether turns, that arrives around turn five without dedicating cards to it.
Hexhaven Dueling Arena is sorcery-speed. Prepare the attacker in your second main phase, after combat, so the free spell is available on the opponent’s turn if it is an instant-speed effect.

title: Rehearsed Ruin
text:
Matchups

Aggro: the deck blocks badly early (1/1s and 2/2s), but Carnivorous Cultivator trades with anything thanks to deathtouch, and Draconic Visitor plus two Heartwoods stabilises fast — 5/5 fliers beat ground decks. Race with Dragons, not with one-drops.
Control: the prepared engine is resilient because the value sits on the battlefield, not in the graveyard or on the stack. A sweeper kills the re-preparers, so hold Codie, Ravenous Codex and Aerid Konstrari until after the first wipe, then rebuild from a board of Heartwood tokens and Pia, Determined Rebuilder.
Midrange: the long game favours this deck. Every turn past six is another free spell, Tarmogoyf gets bigger in both graveyards, and Pia’s pump scales with a board the opponent has to answer every turn.
Heavy artifact removal: Draconic Visitor turns the tokens into creatures before removal can target them, so games where the opponent is holding artifact answers are actually the ones where you want the Dragon line over the mana-rock line.
Fliers and reach: the deck’s clock is aerial, which is a liability against large fliers. Hungering Puppetbeast with trample and Aerid Konstrari’s pump are the answer in those games.

Firebending mana expires at end of combat. It is not end-of-turn mana: any unspent red is gone before your second main phase. Sequence the drains and instants inside combat.
Celebration checks the whole turn. A permanent that enters during the combat step still counts, so a Clue from Azula or an Ally from Sun Warriors keeps Goddric a Dragon after the attack, and the static parts of Grand Ball Guest and Gallant Pie-Wielder stay on through the end step.
Celebration payoffs differ in timing. Goddric, Grand Ball Guest and Gallant Pie-Wielder are continuous, so they are live as soon as the second permanent lands. Ash, Party Crasher checks on attack, which means a Clue made by another attacker during combat does not retroactively grow him: sequence that permanent in the first main phase if you want the counter.
Sun Warriors counts creatures, not power. Token spells cast before combat inflate the mana burst directly, which is why Dragon Fodder and Tinker’s Tote are the best turn-three plays before a Sun Warriors attack.
Firebending Student pumps with prowess. Frontline Rush, Lightning Helix and Silverquill Charm all grow it, and its Firebending X equals its power at the moment it attacks, so casting an instant in the first main phase adds both damage and mana.
Fountainport’s Fish is a token, not an artifact. It counts for Celebration but not for Pactdoll Terror; its Treasure mode is the one that drains.
Acolyte of Aclazotz needs another permanent. It cannot sacrifice itself, so keep a Goblin, Fish, Clue or Tote around as fuel.

title: Sack and Sunder
text:
Early game
The best one-two is Tidings of War into Goblin-town Flunkies or Bothersome Noisemaker. Tidings of War for {R} makes the first Army token, and because amass creates a 0/0 Goblin Army and then puts the counters on it, the token does not die to its own size — it arrives as a 1/1 Goblin. Flunkies then amasses on entry and attacks immediately for 1, and the Noisemaker turns every later cheap spell into another counter event.
Turn three is The Great Goblin whenever possible. He is a 3/2 that blocks, so the turn is not wasted while the board is small, and from the moment he lands every amass in hand is worth 2 damage. If the hand has no Great Goblin, the second-best turn three is Rhovanion Rampager plus a spare one-drop to feed it.
Stony-Voiced Goblins on two is the anti-control opening: a 1/1 that forces a discard is fine to sacrifice later to the Rampager, and taking their sweeper or their answer is worth more than the body.

title: Sack and Sunder
text:
Mid game
Turns four to six are about stacking counter events in a single turn rather than deploying one threat at a time.
The core loop is the Rampager and the Pair together. Attack with the Rampager and sacrifice Fearsome Goblin Pair to its attack trigger: the Rampager gets +1/+1 from a 1/1 and the Pair’s death trigger amasses 4, which is 2 damage and a permanently larger Army. Sacrifice something larger — a Plate Mail–equipped Goblin, a Wargling, or anything that has been pumped — and the Rampager grows by that much instead; its own death trigger then amasses that number, so the deck converts any big creature into an Army of the same size.
Along the Crooked Way is the value card that holds the loop together. It returns a creature card from the graveyard to hand when it enters, which is itself a “creature card leaves your graveyard” trigger for amass 1, and the returned creature is a second sacrifice for the Rampager. It also gives Goblins and Orcs menace for {1}{B} to push the Army through a stalled board.
Keep the Army alive. It is one token shared by every amass card in the deck, so losing it resets the clock; that is the main reason the list plays 24 creatures and only 13 nonland support cards.

title: Sack and Sunder
text:
The combo turn
The engine turn needs three things: The Great Goblin, an Army (or any Goblin) to receive counters, and a hand or graveyard full of cheap counter events.

Start the turn with The Great Goblin and an Army in play. Any amassed Army counts as the Goblin for the counters and as a legal attacker.
Cast Tidings of War for {R}. Amass 1 is 2 damage. Flash it back later for {3}{R} for amass 3, which is 2 more damage off the same card.
Cast Rage into the Valley for {2}{B}: draw a card, lose 1 life, amass 2, 2 damage.
Attack with Rhovanion Rampager, sacrificing whatever is smallest. If the sacrificed creature is Fearsome Goblin Pair, its death trigger amasses 4 — 2 damage — and the Rampager is now a 4/3.
Cast Warg Tactics for {1}{G} targeting the Army: one +1/+1 counter, 2 damage, plus trample and hexproof so the attack connects. Every noncreature spell in this sequence also triggers Bothersome Noisemaker for its own amass and another 2 damage.
Sacrifice Goblin-town for {2}{B}{R}: two more counters, 2 more damage, no card spent.

A realistic turn five with both engines in play is 10 to 14 damage that never needed a big creature, on top of an Army that grew by five or more counters.

title: Sack and Sunder
text:
Win condition 2
The Army is the second win condition, and unlike the burn it needs a board rather than a hand. Every amass card in the list feeds the same token, so an Army that has been through a Goblin-town activation, a flashed-back Tidings of War, one Rampager death and a killed Pair is an 8/8 or larger.
Three cards make it lethal rather than merely large. Wargling gives your whole team trample as soon as you control a creature with power 4 or greater, and the Army qualifies on its own. Goblin Plate Mail gives the equipped Army +1/+0 and menace, which forces two blockers. Warg Tactics grants trample and hexproof for a turn. Between them the Army usually cannot be chump-blocked and cannot be targeted.
The third, quiet path is The Great Goblin’s second ability: every time another Goblin, Orc or Army you control dies, he exiles the top card of your library and lets you play it until the end of your next turn. This deck kills its own creatures on purpose, so in a long game the sacrifices are also card advantage, and the cards they find are more cheap counter events.

title: Sack and Sunder
text:
Key interactions and edge cases







Interaction
Ruling detail




The Great Goblin counts events, not counters
“Whenever you put one or more counters” triggers once no matter how many counters arrive. Fearsome Goblin Pair’s amass 4 is 2 damage, and so is a one-mana Tidings of War


Amass creates the Army first, then adds the counters
With no Army in play, amass creates a 0/0 black Goblin Army token and then puts the counters on it. The token survives because the counters arrive as part of the same instruction


The Army is a Goblin for every other card
Amass makes the token a Goblin, so its counters trigger The Great Goblin, Goblin-town can target it, Plate Mail can attach to it, and it is a legal sacrifice for the Rampager


The Rampager’s counters use the sacrificed creature’s power
Sacrifice a 4-power creature and the Rampager gets four +1/+1 counters, so it is usually worth feeding it the biggest expendable body rather than the smallest


The Rampager’s death trigger reads its power at that moment
Its amass X is the power it had when it died, counters included. A Rampager that ate a 4/4 and then traded is amass 7 — 2 damage and seven counters


Sacrificing to the Rampager happens during the attack declaration
The trigger occurs when it attacks, before blockers, so the sacrificed creature cannot also block. Do not feed it a creature you needed as a blocker


The Great Goblin is legendary
A second copy cannot stay on the battlefield. Play the first and hold the rest; his second ability does not trigger for his own death


The Great Goblin’s exile-play trigger needs a death
It fires when another Goblin, Orc or Army you control dies, and the card is playable until the end of your next turn. Sacrificing on your own turn and casting the exiled card immediately is legal


Along the Crooked Way triggers on any creature card leaving the graveyard
Its own entry trigger returning a creature card to hand counts, so the enchantment amasses 1 the turn it lands. Flashing back Tidings of War does not count — that exiles a sorcery, not a creature card


The menace ability on Along the Crooked Way costs mana every turn
{1}{B} until end of turn for the whole team. Cast it after blocks are declared in a race, or before attacks when the Army needs to force two blockers


Goblin Plate Mail amasses and attaches to the token it makes
The Equipment’s entry trigger amasses 1 and then attaches to that Army, so it is never a dead card with no Goblin in play. Its equip cost is {4}, so the first attachment is the free one that matters


Tidings of War’s flashback is a different size
Amass 1 when cast from hand, amass 3 when cast from the graveyard for {3}{R}, and it is a noncreature spell either way — so Bothersome Noisemaker amasses 1 on top of it


Goblin-town and Mirkwood sacrifice themselves
Both enter tapped and both are cracked for {2} plus a coloured pair of mana. They are the deck’s flood insurance; activating them is a sorcery-speed play, so do it in the second main phase


Mirkwood can only target a Bear, Spider or Wolf
In this list only Rhovanion Rampager and Wargling qualify. Two counters on the Rampager is 2 extra points of amass when it later dies, and two counters on Wargling turns on ferocious for the whole board


Warg Tactics usually wants the counter mode
Destroy target flier is the mode to use against fliers; the counter plus trample and hexproof mode is the one that adds 2 damage through The Great Goblin and pushes the Army through

title: Verdant Liege
text:
Curve and mana
23 lands: 1 Elvenking’s Halls, 3 Thornwood Falls, 2 Temple of Mystery, 2 Mutant Town, 2 Strangled Cemetery, 2 Subterranean Cavern, 2 Murky Sewer, 4 Forest, 3 Island, 2 Swamp. Green sources 13, blue sources 12, black sources 6. Ten of the lands enter tapped unconditionally and four more (Strangled Cemetery and Murky Sewer) enter tapped until a player is at thirteen or less life, which is why the deck starts on turn two and wants a green source in every opening hand.
Nonland curve: one-drop x2, two-drops x6, three-drops x11, four-drops x11, five-drops x2, six-drops x4, seven-drop x1. Average nonland CMC 3.57. The deck is creature-dense at thirty-four creatures plus three sagas, so it is never short of a landfall trigger to put counters on. Playing two lands per turn from Thranduil’s Company is the single biggest upgrade the deck has: it doubles the number of triggers per turn cycle and effectively adds a mana per turn.

title: Verdant Liege
text:
Early game
Turn one is a land, and the only true one-drop is Most Decrepit Old Bird, which is a 1/1 flier that mills you towards threshold with its Adventure. Turn two is where the deck commits to a colour pair: Woodland Weavemaster is the best green follow-up because it is a mana Elf that grows, Attercop is the best defensive one, and Old Thrush is the fixing play that guarantees a land on top.
Do not play Mirkwood Pathmaker early if you have something else to do. It is a tiny creature on turn three with three lands and a real threat on turn six with six, so it is a finisher you hold until the land count is real.

title: Verdant Liege
text:
Mid game
Turn three to five is when Thranduil, Sindarin Liege and Thranduil’s Company turn the board into a machine. The order matters: cast the lord first so the tokens he makes are already 2/2 with his anthem, then the Company, so that the Company’s additional-land clause starts applying on the turn it resolves. Down in the Valley bridges the two by tutoring the land you need and then granting the board its own token clause on chapter two.
The land count is the scoreboard. Count your lands before every attack: with Thranduil’s Company and Down in the Valley out, each land drop is a token, two counters and a vigilance attacker, and Wood Elves, Old Thrush, Silvan Reveler, Gone Fishing and Down in the Valley’s first chapter all put lands into play from hand, library, graveyard or exile.

title: Verdant Liege
text:
The combo turn

Land count check, then land drop one. If Thranduil’s Company is on the board and you control another Elf, take the second land drop in the same turn.
Resolve each landfall trigger in the order that matters: put the two +1/+1 counters from Thranduil’s Company on the creature that is actually being blocked, not the token.
Add triggers from hand: Wood Elves (a Forest onto the battlefield), Silvan Reveler (discard a land, return it tapped), Old Thrush (a basic on top of the library) or Gone Fishing (two of your lands leave and return).
Sacrifice Elvenking’s Halls for two more counters once the board is stable and the coloured mana is no longer needed. Two counters on an evasive Elf is usually the difference between a stall and a kill.
Attack with the vigilance team. Down in the Valley’s chapters three and four give +1/+0 and vigilance, so the same creatures that made the tokens also attack and still block.

A worked example: Thranduil, Sindarin Liege on board, Thranduil’s Company on board, four lands. Play a land (token plus two counters on the Company), play the extra land from the Company (a second token plus two more counters), then cast Silvan Reveler and pitch a land (a third token, and the pitched land returns tapped). That is four Elf tokens, four +1/+1 counters and a 3/4 or 4/4 Company attacking on turn five, and the lord has not attacked yet.

title: Verdant Liege
text:
Win condition 2
When the ground clogs with tokens, the lands themselves finish the game. Mirkwood Pathmaker is a three-mana creature whose power and toughness equal your land count, so in a deck that plays two lands per turn it is routinely a 6/6 or 7/7 for three. Attack with it while Thranduil’s Company’s landfall counters and Elvenking’s Halls’ sacrifice counters pile up, and it stops being blockable by anything reasonable.
The backup is Gigantic Big Bear: seven mana for a ten-power hasty hexproof creature that cannot be countered. It comes down the turn after a wipe, ignores the sweepers that hit the token swarm, and does not need the lord or a single counter to be lethal. The Notary Hobbits exists for the opposite situation: when you are short of mana for those finishers, it enters as three Halflings and taps for one colourless mana each, which pays for the Elf-restricted mana Woodland Weavemaster produces.

title: Verdant Liege
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep two to four lands with at least two green sources, and at least one play at two or three mana. The ideal opener is a Forest or Thornwood Falls, a second land, Woodland Weavemaster or Attercop, and one of Thranduil, Sindarin Liege, Thranduil’s Company, or Down in the Valley. Mulligan hands with fewer than two lands, hands with no green source, hands with three or more copies of the six-drop slot and no cheap play, and hands whose only blue source is Temple of Mystery if the curve depends on Mirkwood Meditator or Elrond, Moon-Reader. Because fifteen of the lands enter tapped in the early turns, value hands that go tapped dual into basic two-drop; do not keep a hand that needs untapped blue on turn three and cannot get it.

title: Verdant Liege
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Thranduil, Sindarin Liege’s token clause is a triggered ability with the landfall trigger, so the token arrives after the land. Token Elves get +1/+1 from his own anthem, which makes them 2/2, and they trigger Woodland Weavemaster’s growth on entry.
Thranduil’s Company’s additional land drop requires you to control another Elf. Play the Company second, not first, or the extra land is wasted for the turn.
The extra land drop and Down in the Valley’s tutored land do not conflict: the tutor puts the basic into hand, the extra drop plays it, and both generate landfall triggers.
Down in the Valley’s chapter two grants the saga itself a permanent landfall clause, so the tokens keep coming on chapters three and four as well. Chapter one is a basic land to hand, not onto the battlefield, so it does not trigger landfall on its own.
Silvan Reveler’s recursion clause costs one green one blue and returns it from the graveyard to your hand, not to the battlefield. Casting it again is a second enter trigger and a second loot, which is how the deck grinds through removal.
Gone Fishing exiles two creatures or lands you control and returns them at the same time, so a land returned this way triggers landfall twice, and an Elf returned this way enters twice for Woodland Weavemaster and Boughside Wanderers.
Thranduil, the Elvenking copies activated abilities, not triggered abilities, from Elves in your graveyard. Woodland Weavemaster’s mana ability and any future Elf’s activated ability are the targets; the lord’s own landfall token clause is not.
Elrond, Moon-Reader draws only once each turn and only from a creature’s activated ability, so activate Woodland Weavemaster on your second main phase if you are also casting spells, not before combat.
Mirkwood Pathmaker’s power is a characteristic-defining ability, not a trigger: it counts lands at all times, including lands that enter after it is on the board, so the extra land from Thranduil’s Company makes it bigger immediately.
Elvenking’s Halls enters tapped. Play it on a turn when your curve is already complete, and sacrifice it only when the counters matter more than the green and blue source.
Most Decrepit Old Bird’s threshold needs seven cards in a graveyard, which Silvan Rally and Speak Secrets both work towards.

Interaction
Ruling detail




Recruit is one trigger with two outcomes
Draw, then discard, then if the discarded card was a nonland, create the Soldier. Discarding a land is not a failure — with 23 lands, recruit is also how the deck filters floods, and Lakeshore Apothecary and Ravenhill Flock count the draw either way


The Queen of Dale triggers once per turn
Only the opponent’s first noncreature spell each turn recruits. Extra noncreature spells later in the same turn do nothing, so do not hold the Queen expecting a second trigger


Gollum, Riddle Master’s parity is locked in
Odd or even is chosen as he enters and never changes, zero counts as even, and each of the three outcomes can be chosen only once. Name even against decks built on two-mana interaction, odd against decks built on one- and three-mana spells


Gollum the Abandoned’s recursion is sorcery speed
The {2} plus a sacrifice can only be activated on your turn, and it returns him to hand rather than the battlefield, so he has to be replayed. Sacrificing a Soldier token or a spent Great Gilded Boat costs nothing the deck misses


Lake-town Toymaker checks before combat
The two-card condition is checked at the beginning of combat. Trigger a recruit in your first main phase, or hold Sound the Trumpets, rather than relying on the draw step alone


Great Gilded Boat recruits on any attack
The trigger is on attacking, not on the Boat attacking, and it does not require the Boat to be crewed. The 4/4 body is a bonus; the card and the token are the point, and the Boat is also the cheapest sacrifice for Gollum’s recursion once it has done its job


Esgaroth Garrison counts itself
Its power is a characteristic-defining ability equal to the number of creatures you control, so it enters as at least a 2/5 even on an empty board and grows with every Soldier token


Magnificent End’s discount
It costs {3} less only if the target is already tapped when you cast it, which makes it a one-mana answer to anything that attacked you and a five-mana answer to a blocker


Sound the Trumpets recruits conditionally
The recruit only happens if the countered spell had mana value 2 or less. It is a tempo play against cheap interaction, not a hard counter for a five-drop


The Eagles Are Coming! timing
The Bird tokens are created at the beginning of the next upkeep, so they attack on your following turn. Returning a creature is a real cost, which is why it should return ETB creatures such as Patient Instructor or Long Lake Nuisance that recruit again on replay


Rogue’s Passage has no timing restriction
{4}, {T} can be activated in the declare-blockers step, after the opponent has committed blockers, and the {4} can be paid with any colour

Eerie triggers only on enchantments you control. The deck’s enchantments are Lightwheel Enhancements, Nowhere to Run and Momentum Breaker — the Disguise creatures are creatures, not enchantments, and turning one face up is not an enchantment entering.
Speed does not go up on its own: it increases once on each of your turns when an opponent loses life. Balemurk Leech’s drain is the most reliable trigger because it does not need a successful attack, and life loss from the drain counts even if it happens during your end step.
A face-down Disguise creature is a 2/2 with no name, no types and ward 2. Unyielding Gatekeeper is an Elephant Cleric once flipped, not a Detective, and the flip is a special action you can take at any time you could cast an instant.

Nowhere to Run switches off hexproof and ward for your removal for as long as it stays on the battlefield, and its own -3/-3 effect is a permanent shrink, not a damage effect, so it also answers indestructible creatures by killing the ones with 3 or less toughness.
Lightwheel Enhancements at max speed can be cast from the graveyard, but it is an Aura: you need a creature or Vehicle to enchant, so keep one alive before you spend the mana.

Bitter Triumph’s additional cost is a discard or 3 life. Discard a second copy of a legendary card, an extra land or a Lightwheel Enhancements you plan to cast from the graveyard later.

The manabase has no dual lands, so count coloured sources: 6 white, 7 black, 5 blue, and six lands that produce only colourless mana. Sequence the colourless lands after your coloured ones unless you are actually casting a face-down creature.
The Speed Demon’s draw trigger costs life equal to your speed. At speed 4 that is four life every turn, so do not flip the Demon on at 6 life and expect to survive your own end step.
