title: Tidepool Tithe
text:
Overview
Tidepool Tithe is built on one piece of rules text: “While paying a waterbend cost, you can tap your artifacts and creatures to help. Each one pays for {1}.” Three mechanics are wired into that sentence.
Lifegain is the fuel. Wanderbrine Preacher gains 2 life every time it becomes tapped, Compassionate Healer gains 1 and scrys, and Hinterland Sanctifier gains 1 whenever any other creature enters. Marauding Blight-Priest and Enduring Tenacity convert each of those gains straight into opponent life loss, so the life you gain while paying costs is also the damage that closes the game.
Waterbending is the engine. Every waterbend cost in the deck sits on a card you already want: Katara, Water Tribe’s Hope; Katara, Bending Prodigy; Waterbender Ascension; Crashing Wave; Waterbending Lesson; Ruinous Waterbending and Aang’s Iceberg. Paying a cost is therefore never a wasted tap, because the creatures you tap are the ones that reward being tapped.
Impending is the resilience. The Overlords enter for a cheap impending cost as noncreature enchantments with time counters, blanking sorcery-speed creature removal and creature wipes, then become 5/5 or 6/6 bodies a few turns later. Overlord of the Balemurk mills four and returns a creature card to hand, reloading the engine; Overlord of the Mistmoors makes two evasive tokens the turn it lands, even while it is not yet a creature.
This is a midrange machine rather than a two-card infinite combo: the “combo” is a repeatable tap loop, and it usually kills between turns 6 and 8 through drips, drains and one large attack.

title: Tidepool Tithe
text:
Approach

Game plan phases
Turns 1-3 — Establish bodies. Deploy the cheapest lifegain creatures: Hinterland Sanctifier, Wanderbrine Preacher, Compassionate Healer. These are not attack pressure; they are the payment source for every waterbend cost and the trigger source for every drain payoff.

Patrol turns a one-shot tap into a two-a-turn loop: tap Preacher for a waterbend cost, untap it with Patrol, tap it again. title: Tidepool Tithe
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Lead with lifegain bodies over card draw. Hinterland Sanctifier on turn 1 and Wanderbrine Preacher on turn 2 is the ideal opening: the Preacher is the deck’s cheapest repeatable waterbend payment, and the Sanctifier turns every later token into another life gain. Against aggressive opponents, Compassionate Healer plus Aang’s Iceberg on flash buys the turns you need.


Mid game
This is where the loop comes online. With a Preacher plus a Blight-Priest or Enduring Tenacity in play, every waterbend cost you pay is damage. Use Katara, Bending Prodigy’s waterbend {6} to draw cards by tapping three creatures and paying three mana, or pay six mana and keep the board untapped for blocks. North Pole Patrol then untaps the best tap-payoff creature, so the same Preacher can gain life twice in one turn cycle.


The combo turn

Board: Wanderbrine Preacher, Compassionate Healer, North Pole Patrol, Katara WTH (or Katara, Bending Prodigy), Marauding Blight-Priest, five or six lands.
Activate Katara, Water Tribe’s Hope’s waterbend {X} for X = 5, paying by tapping Preacher, Compassionate Healer, Patrol, Katara’s Ally token and one more body.
Those taps fire Preacher (gain 2) and Healer (gain 1), which makes Blight-Priest and/or Enduring Tenacity drain 3 to 5 life before combat.
Every creature you control is now base 5/5 (Katara herself included, and she has vigilance, so she pseudo-attacks and still got tapped for value).
Attack with the team, or first clear the way with Crashing Wave’s waterbend {X} to tap blockers and stun them for three turns.

Note that X may be paid with any mix of mana and taps. A hand with 6 mana and only two creatures can still waterbend {X} for 6.


Win condition 2
Restless Reef plus waterbend aggression. Two Reefs each become 4/4 deathtouch Sharks for {2}{U}{B}, which is a real clock that ignores creature sweepers and block-based removal, and each attack mills four cards for Overlord of the Balemurk. Waterbender Ascension’s waterbend {4} grants unblockable to whichever creature actually matters, and Giant-style unblockable tricks are irrelevant to the Reef because deathtouch plus a 4/4 body forces bad blocks anyway. The drain loop usually finishes what the Reef starts.


Mulligan guide
Keep: 2-4 lands including at least one white source, one or two one- and two-drop lifegain creatures, and either a payoff (Blight-Priest, Enduring Tenacity) or a waterbend engine card (Katara WTH, North Pole Patrol, Waterbender Ascension).
Ship: hands with zero creatures, hands with both Katara, Water Tribe’s Hope and Overlord of the Mistmoors and no action before turn 4, and any hand with fewer than two lands. Six-card hands are fine; the deck is redundant by design and drawn by Waterbending Lesson, Katara, Bending Prodigy and Overlord of the Floodpits.


Key interactions and edge cases

Waterbend costs are paid by tapping, or by mana, or both. Each artifact or creature pays for {1}; nothing forces you to tap. Katara, Bending Prodigy’s waterbend {6} for a card is frequently best paid as three mana plus three taps.
Tapped creatures cannot pay twice. Already-tapped bodies are not available, which is why North Pole Patrol (untap another target permanent) is a genuine engine card.
Vigilance creatures attack and still tap. Katara WTH, Flexible-style vigilance bodies and the Ally token are the best payment sources because attacking costs them nothing.
Ruinous Waterbending kills your own small bodies. Minus two toughness removes Hinterland Sanctifier (1/2) and Wanderbrine Preacher (2/2); Katara, Bending Prodigy (2/3) and North Pole Patrol (2/3) live. Cast it when the exchange favours you, and pay the waterbend {4} so that every creature that dies this turn, including your own, gains you 1 life.
Enduring Tenacity survives sweepers. When it dies as a creature it returns to the battlefield as a noncreature enchantment, so the drain trigger keeps working after a wipe.
Impending dodges removal. While time counters remain, the Overlord is an enchantment, not a creature: it cannot be attacked profitably, is immune to “destroy target creature” and to sorcery-speed wipes, and cannot be tapped for waterbend. The end step that removes the last counter is when it becomes a creature, so it can attack on the following turn.
Overlord of the Mistmoors while impending. Its entry trigger makes two 2/1 flying Insects even though the Overlord itself is not yet a creature; those tokens gain you two life via Hinterland Sanctifier and can pay two toward any waterbend cost.
Crashing Wave timing. Waterbend {X} is an additional cost, so X is locked in as you cast it. Tap the creatures you want to remove, then stack the three stun counters on whatever also has to be kept down.
Aang’s Iceberg is a blink-style answer. Exiling a permanent keeps it exiled only while the Iceberg stays; its waterbend {3} sacrifice mode is what makes it permanent, so only use it on something you never want back.



Matchups
Aggro. Favourable: cheap blockers, three lands that gain life, Ruinous Waterbending as a reset and the drain loop all line up well; the danger is a fast flying start, answered by Aang’s Iceberg and Crashing Wave.
Control. Slightly favourable: Overlords ignore wraths, Enduring Tenacity returns from the graveyard and Blight-Priest punishes anyone who taps out.
Midrange. Even to favourable: the deck out-grinds on card flow and Katara WTH’s pump ends stalls, but do not trade drain payoffs into removal for no value.
Combo. Unfavourable before sideboarding: the plan is speed plus disruption, using Crashing Wave and Aang’s Iceberg while Overlords and Reefs pressure the kill.

title: Hoardmouth
text:
Overview
Hoardmouth is built on one blunt rules interaction: Draconic Visitor replaces every artifact token you create with a 5/5 red Dragon token with flying. The deck is therefore a pile of cheap Treasure production, and each Treasure is really a Dragon once the Visitor is on the battlefield. Gold Rush, Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant, Charming Scoundrel, Rapacious Dragon, Bonehoard Dracosaur and even The Gold Saucer all read “make a Treasure” until the Visitor rewrites them.
Behold is the connective tissue. Sarkhan wants a Dragon revealed to pay for his Treasure. Molten Exhale gets flash, Piercing Exhale adds surveil 2 and Dispelling Exhale demands {4} instead of {2} when a Dragon is beheld. Because half the deck is Dragons, the additional costs are free, and revealing a Dragon is never a cost you actually pay.
The payoff layer is Lathliss, Dragon Queen (a 5/5 token for every nontoken Dragon that enters) and Dragonstorm Globe (every Dragon enters with an extra +1/+1 counter). A single Rapacious Dragon then produces three extra bodies: its two hatching Treasures and Lathliss’s token. That is 18 power across four fliers for five mana.
Deck average mana value is 3.25 across 36 nonland cards, with 24 lands. The plan wants four lands on turn four and a Visitor by turn five, then a burst turn.

title: Hoardmouth
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Turns one through three are about lands and a two-drop. Sarkhan is the best opening: he beholds a Dragon from hand, makes a Treasure, and turns into a 2/2 flier with a +1/+1 counter the moment your first Dragon lands. Charming Scoundrel is the flexible option, filtering on a land-heavy hand or making the Treasure outright. Hold Molten Exhale rather than firing it at the first creature; four damage at instant speed is your answer to the format’s two- and three-drops and it costs the same either way.


Mid game and the combo turn
Resolve Draconic Visitor before anything else. Everything after it is a burst turn: Gold Rush for two mana, Sarkhan’s Treasure, Rapacious Dragon’s two Treasures, Bonehoard Dracosaur’s upkeep Treasure. The correct sequence on a burst turn is Visitor, then Dragonstorm Globe if you have it, then as many Treasure sources as mana allows, because the Globe’s counter applies to the tokens as they are created. Five lands with a Visitor and two Gold Rush is 10 power of flying on turn five from two cards already on the table.
Roiling Dragonstorm is the draw engine that keeps this going. Cast it, draw two and discard the worst card, then play any Dragon and it returns to your hand. Each replay is two fresh cards for two mana, and the deck’s Dragon count means the rebuy happens almost every turn.


The combo turn in detail
Brass’s Bounty is the ceiling. With seven lands and a Visitor, it makes seven Dragons for seven mana, and with a Globe those are 8/8 fliers. That is the turn where a stalled board becomes lethal; do not fire it early for value, because without the Visitor it is only a pile of Treasures you cannot use the same turn.


Win condition two
Firespitter Whelp plus Lathliss is the grind plan. Every noncreature spell and every Dragon spell drains each opponent for one, and Lathliss makes the Dragon count climb on its own. Against decks that answer individual fliers, the drain finishes what the swarm starts. Kiora of Fire and Ashes is the long-game reset: a 5/5 on entry, then eight mana for another every turn once the board is stable.


Mulligan guide
Keep hands with three or four lands, at least two mana sources of the same color as your cheapest spell, and either a two-drop or a Visitor. Ship hands that have no Dragon to behold and no way to make Treasure, because both Sarkhan and the Exhale cycle are dead without one. A hand of five lands, Draconic Visitor and Lathliss is a keep on the play; the same hand with no red source is not.


Key interactions

Beholding is not a sacrifice. Revealing a Dragon card from hand satisfies the cost, so Sarkhan and the Exhales never cost you a permanent.
Lathliss triggers only on nontoken Dragons, which here means Draconic Visitor, Rapacious Dragon and Bonehoard Dracosaur. Visitor-made 5/5s are tokens and do not multiply themselves, and Kiora’s Dragon is also a token, so it does not trigger her.
Dragonstorm Globe’s counter applies to Dragon tokens created after it resolves, including Visitor’s 5/5s.
Draconic Visitor is a replacement effect, not a trigger. It applies to the Treasure from The Gold Saucer and from any source, and it also stops Treasure from being sacrificed for mana because the Treasure is never created.
Piercing Exhale uses the creature’s power at resolution, so fire it after the Globe counters or a Lathliss pump for the biggest fight.
Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon can only pay for Dragon spells, which means the Visitor, Lathliss, Rapacious Dragon, Bonehoard Dracosaur, Kiora and Sarkhan, not for Gold Rush or the Exhales.

title: Graveyard Shift

Win condition 2
When the board is stalled, the deck wins without attacking. With twenty-five noncreature spells, and with the same triggers repeated through flashback, that is a steady clock that ignores blockers, lifegain on the ground and combat math entirely. Red Mage’s Rapier’s bearer also grows by +2/+0 on each of those spells, so the turn spent draining also builds the attacker that ends the game.
The third route is the manlands. Restless Fortress hits for 1 and drains 2 while gaining 2, which is a two-point swing every attack, and Restless Vents attacks as a 2/3 with menace and loots on every swing. Both lands are immune to sorcery-speed creature removal after the fact and can be activated after a sweeper has cleared the token board, which makes them the most reliable threat in long games.

Keep any two- or three-land hand that contains one engine piece and one token spell. title: Graveyard Shift
text:

Job select attaches for free: the Equipment enters, the Hero token is created, and the Equipment is attached to it in the same resolution, so no equip cost is ever paid for the first attachment.
Ravenous Robots counts artifact spells, not artifacts, so each job-select Equipment and each copied Equipment triggers it once for a 1/1 Robot.
Warleader’s Call triggers on tokens as well as creatures, so every job-select Hero, every Robot and every Spirit is another point of damage to the opponent.
Antiquities on the Loose is better out of the graveyard than from hand: casting it from anywhere other than your hand gives both Spirits a +1/+1 counter.
The Final Days scales with the graveyard, and because the deck plays eleven creatures plus its own discarded spells, the flashed-back version usually creates more than two Horrors.
Electroduplicate’s copy is sacrificed at the end step, so it is a haste attacker and a Warleader’s Call trigger, not a permanent.
Group Project’s flashback cost is tapping three untapped creatures, which the job-select Equipment provides for free; attack with the tokens first, then flash it back in the second main phase.
Black Mage’s Rod and Mysidian Elder’s token both say each opponent, so they scale in multiplayer-style board states and cannot be blocked or redirected.
Rogue’s Passage adds colourless mana, so it can be played on turn one without breaking the curve and cashed in later as the finisher.
Restless Fortress and Restless Vents enter tapped, so sequence them on a turn when the mana is not needed.

title: Landwarp

Overview
Landwarp fuses three mechanics into one combat engine. Landfall turns every land drop into power and board growth (Tifa Lockhart doubles her power, Mossborn Hydra doubles its counters, Mightform Harmonizer doubles any creature’s power, Eusocial Engineering and Felidar Retreat add bodies). Warp is the recursion half: every warp card can be cast from hand for a discount, is exiled at the next end step, and can be cast again from exile on a later turn, so engines like Mightform Harmonizer and Eusocial Engineering keep returning. Sneak is the surprise-attack half: when you have an unblocked attacker, you return it to hand during the declare blockers step and cast a Sneak card for its sneak cost — creatures enter tapped and attacking, which is how Michelangelo, Improviser lands on the board mid-combat and starts dumping lands and creatures from your hand.
The three mechanics reinforce each other. Michelangelo’s combat damage trigger plays an extra land and an extra creature, which feeds Landfall payoffs on the same turn they attack. Raphael, the Nightwatcher gives all attackers double strike, so a Landfall-doubled Tifa or Hydra ends games in one swing. Dark Leo and Shredder turn the ninja count into a second, independent kill: every combat with five or more Ninjas (turtles and spirit tokens included) makes the opponent lose half their remaining life.

The nonland curve averages 3.1 CMC (1.9 counting lands), with most expensive pieces playable at a discount: warp costs run one to three mana below the printed cost, and sneak costs are even cheaper on a developed board. The manabase is 24 lands: eleven basics for the verge conditions, six verge duals covering every color pair, Restless Cottage, and four fetch lands that double as landfall triggers. New Generation’s Technique (sneak {2}{G}) is effectively a fifth ramp spell that fetches two basics tapped and fires two landfall triggers.

title: Landwarp
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Prioritize land drops over everything: Sazh’s Chocobo and Tifa Lockhart grow on every landfall, so the first three turns are about curving lands and cheap green threats. Splinter, Hamato Yoshi is the best two-drop: menace is your most reliable source of unblocked attackers for sneak costs, and it pumps the other Ninjas. If the opener has a warp engine (Mightform Harmonizer or Eusocial Engineering), warp-cast it cheaply: it will be exiled at end step and come back next turn, giving a second round of landfall triggers.


Mid game
Set up the kill: keep an engine on the board, hold a land in hand for Michelangelo, and attack with the ninja package. Do not overextend into sweepers; All-Fates Stalker and Shredder’s Technique keep the opponent’s blockers and bombs honest, and Splinter’s Technique fetches exactly the piece the board state needs.


The combo turn

Attack with a ninja or menace creature.
If it is unblocked, return it to hand in the declare blockers step and cast Michelangelo, Improviser for its sneak cost {2}{G}{G}; he enters tapped and attacking.
Michelangelo’s combat damage lets you put a creature card and/or a land card from hand onto the battlefield.
The extra land drop fires every Landfall ability: Tifa and Hydra double, Mightform doubles another creature’s power, Eusocial makes a Robot, Felidar Retreat makes a Cat or pumps the team.
With Raphael, the Nightwatcher also attacking, all attackers have double strike; Restless Cottage and Robots add the final points.



Win condition 2: the ninja swarm
Dark Leo and Shredder creates a 1/1 Ninja token every time it deals combat damage, and each such trigger checks the ninja count: if you control five or more Ninjas, the opponent loses half their life, rounded up. Turtles and Splinter are Ninjas, The Last Ronin’s Technique’s three Spirits are Ninja Turtle Spirits, and every Dark Leo hit adds another token, so two solid combat steps with the swarm end the game regardless of the landfall math.


Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two or three lands and a cheap threat (Sazh’s Chocobo, Tifa, Splinter). Keep hands with a warp engine plus enough lands to cast it or warp it by turn three. Ship hands that are all four-drops or missing color sources for their early cards; the deck wants to use its lands every turn.


Key interactions and edge cases

Sneak requires an unblocked attacker: if your only attacker is blocked, you cannot pay sneak costs that turn. Menace (Splinter) and evasive tokens are the safety valves.
Warped permanents are exiled at the beginning of the next end step and can be cast from exile later, so warp is not a one-shot discount: it is a repeatable engine, and warp costs can be paid again each turn.
All-Fates Stalker exiles a non-Assassin creature until it leaves the battlefield; warp-casting it each turn gives repeatable exile removal.
Michelangelo’s trigger is optional (“you may”), and you can choose only a creature, only a land, or both.
The Last Ronin’s Technique’s Spirits enter tapped and attacking only when the sneak cost was paid; cast normally they are just three chump-blockers/attackers.
Weftstalker Ardent pings each opponent for every creature or artifact that enters under your control, so token-making turns (Eusocial Robots, Felidar Cats, Dark Leo Ninjas, Last Ronin Spirits) double as reach.
Shredder’s Technique destroys enchantments too, and you lose 2 life only if it destroys an enchantment.



Matchups
Against aggro, block early with Felidar Retreat Cats and Sazh’s Chocobo, and use Shredder’s Technique and Jennika-style tempo to stabilize; lifegain from Restless Cottage Food and the Cat token race matters. Against midrange, warp recursion out-values them: engines keep coming back from exile while their one-for-one removal runs dry. Against control, spread the clock: Ninja tokens and Restless Cottage survive sweepers as lands, Splinter’s Technique finds the finisher, and Raphael plus double strike punishes tapped-out turns. The deck’s weakness is fast combo and wide flyer strategies, where the manabase’s tapped fetch lands cost a tempo turn.

title: Mirkwood Menagerie
text:
Overview
Mirkwood Menagerie is the ninth dedicated daily Hobbit combo deck. Eight earlier builds claimed the set’s headline engines — the storied dwarves, the goblin amass raid, the elvenking’s court, Smaug’s hoard, the wilderland pack, the Lake-town recruits, the dwarf bards and the thieves of the crooked way — so today’s deck takes the wild remnants of the set and makes them cohere: wolves, bears, a rabbit, a bee, Mirkwood elves, an eagle and a border garrison. The unused Hobbit pool is thin (18 cards, all common/uncommon), so the deck is fused around the two mechanics those leftovers share: Ferocious (Rabbit and Warg pay off power 4 or greater) and Landfall (Raft-Steerer and the Mirkwood druids trigger off every land), held together by a +1/+1 counter subtheme and a token-swarm finish.
The engine chain is simple but deep: small creatures (and the tokens they make) draw cards through Enduring Innocence; big creatures (Ordinary Bear, a pumped Guardian of the Halls, a grown Elvish Refueler, Ojer Taq) draw cards through Outcaster Trailblazer; Mirkwood Nurturer bounces a creature or land to re-trigger entries and landfall; and every creature on the board feeds Esgaroth Garrison’s power. Then Ojer Taq, Deepest Foundation triples every token — soldiers, heroes and roles — and Zanarkand’s adventure lands a Hero token with a +1/+1 counter for each land you control.

Turn ferocious on (turns 3–5). Ordinary Bear (4/5) and Guardian of the Halls’ {5}{G}{G} pump are the reliable enablers; Elvish Refueler grows past 4 power with spare mana; every big entry draws via Outcaster Trailblazer. Elven Raft-Steerer taps blockers on landfall, buying time.
Stampede (turns 5+). Esgaroth Garrison’s power equals your creature count; Eagle of the Great Shelf and a solved Case of the Gateway Express anthem the board; Rabbit Response is a +2/+1 finisher with scry 2 (you control a Rabbit). title: Mirkwood Menagerie
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Turn 1 Nasty Little Rabbit, turn 2 any two-drop. Prefer Guardian of the Halls and Ravening Warg — they win the ground while Duskwatch Hunter’s counter and token-evasion apply pressure. Enduring Innocence on turn 3 turns every subsequent small creature into a card. The duals enter tapped, so sequence basics first on turns 1–2.


Mid game
Establish ferocious: Ordinary Bear or a {5}{G}{G} pump on Guardian of the Halls. From here Outcaster Trailblazer draws on every big entry, and Mirkwood Nurturer can bounce a spent creature (or an ETB-tapped land) to re-trigger entries and landfall. Elven Raft-Steerer taps the biggest blocker each landfall, letting wolves and bears through.


The combo turn

Enduring Innocence + Outcaster Trailblazer convert every creature you cast into a card — the swarm refuels itself.
Mirkwood Nurturer bounces and replays a creature (or a land) for extra counters, draws and landfall taps.
Ojer Taq, Deepest Foundation triples every token: Esgaroth’s recruit Soldier, Castle Guard’s Hero, Royal Treatment’s Role — each token maker now makes three bodies.
Swing with the full board: Esgaroth Garrison is huge from the creature count, Eagle of the Great Shelf anthems per attacker, Case of the Gateway Express is solved (+1/+0), and Rabbit Response gives +2/+1 and scry 2.



Win condition 2 — the giant Hero
Cast Lasting Fayth from Zanarkand, Ancient Metropolis when you control a dozen or more lands: the Hero token enters with that many +1/+1 counters. Royal Treatment and Duskwatch Hunter counters stack on it. The token wins through sheer size — protect it with Royal Treatment and finish over two turns.


Win condition 3 — the Wolf stampede
Banner of Kinship enters naming Wolf with a fellowship counter for each Wolf you control — up to seven (three Ravening Warg, three Duskwatch Hunter, one Desolation Prowler) — turning every Wolf into a 9/9-plus threat. It is a one-card finisher that also works as a giant pump for the wolf half of the board.


Mulligan guide

Keep: 2–3 lands with a green source, a two-drop, and ideally a Rabbit or Guardian.
Ship: one-landers, five-plus-land hands, and hands with double-white or double-black spells but no matching source.
Keep Outcaster Trailblazer or Enduring Innocence hands on a playable curve — the engines beat raw stats.
The ETB-tapped duals slow the first two turns: an opening of three tapped duals is a mulligan.



Key interactions and edge cases

Enduring Innocence triggers only once per turn — time your token bursts (Esgaroth recruit, Castle Guard death) to your own turn.
Outcaster Trailblazer draws only on power 4 or greater entries — the ferocious enablers (Ordinary Bear, Guardian pump, Refueler growth) are what turn it on.
Banner of Kinship chooses a type at entry — name Wolf; the fellowship counter count is set when it enters, so cast it when your wolf count is highest.
Ojer Taq triples tokens, not counters — the +1/+1 counters from Duskwatch Hunter, Troll Negotiations and Refueler are unaffected (a good thing: they stack on tripled bodies).
Zanarkand is a land and a spell — cast Lasting Fayth from hand, then play Zanarkand from exile later; the land face enters tapped.
Ojer Taq’s death returns it transformed as Temple of Civilization, a land; {2}{W}, {T} transforms it back after attacking with three or more creatures — the win condition loops itself.
Liminal Hold exiles until it leaves — it handles any nonland permanent, including enchantments and artifacts.
Mirkwood Nurturer can bounce a land — replay it for an extra landfall trigger (Raft-Steerer tap-down).
Case of the Gateway Express solves at your end step after three or more creatures attacked — the +1/+0 is permanent once solved.



Matchups

Aggro: Ravening Warg deathtouch and Raft-Steerer landfall taps hold the ground; Great Fierce Bee and Velvetwing Butterflies block flyers; Liminal Hold exiles the biggest threat.
Midrange: Outcaster Trailblazer’s card advantage out-draws them; Troll Negotiations and Bushwhack fights trade up; Banner of Kinship and Ojer Taq outclass their top end.
Control: Enduring Innocence and Trailblazer refill after sweepers; Royal Treatment protects Ojer Taq; Zanarkand’s giant Hero token is a single-card clock they can’t answer cheaply.

title: Molten Mint
text:
Curve and mana
24 lands: 4 The Lonely Mountain, 10 Mountain, 5 Swamp, 5 Forest. Red sources 14, black 5, green 5, and every Treasure token in the deck is a wildcard source on top of that.
Nonland curve: 1-drop x2, 2-drop x11, 3-drop x10, 4-drop x9, 5-drop x4. Average nonland CMC 3.06. The deck wants a two-drop hoard piece on turn two, a Treasure maker on turn three, and Smaug the Magnificent on turn four with at least two Treasures already banked. There are no one-mana plays other than Stir Up Trouble, which is deliberate: the deck spends its early turns building, not attacking.

title: Molten Mint
text:
Early game
Turns one and two belong to the hoard. Gold Pan is the ideal turn-two play in a list this greedy: it creates a Treasure, it is an Equipment (so The Lonely Mountain comes in untapped), and it discounts the Mountain’s Dwarf-token ability by one. Piggy Bank is the aggressive alternative — a 3/2 that turns into a Treasure when it dies, which makes every block profitable. The Sackville-Bagginses is the engine piece: feed it any spare artifact, draw a card, make a Treasure, and from that point on every Treasure you crack for mana also drains the opponent for 1.
Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant is the quiet setup card. Beholding a Dragon in hand costs nothing, produces a Treasure on entry, and turns Sarkhan into a growing Dragon the moment a real Dragon lands.
Do not chain-cast for value yet. Hold Stir Up Trouble as a one-mana answer; its additional cost is any artifact or creature, so a spent Treasure doubles as the removal spell’s fuel.

title: Molten Mint
text:
Mid game
Turns three through five are when the hoard becomes a threat. The Misty Mountains Cold is the centerpiece: a Treasure on every chapter, and as soon as the count reaches four the Saga sacrifices itself for a 6/6 flying Dragon token. Because it checks after each chapter, a board with Dori and a Plundering Pirate already running can flip the Dragon on chapter two.
Flamekin Gildweaver, Plundering Pirate and Redcap Thief keep the board populated while they raise the hoard. Rapacious Dragon is where the phase peaks: two Treasures and a 3/3 flyer, and the Treasures pay for the next Dragon.
Desolation of Smaug is the reset button. It deals three to each non-Dragon creature, which kills almost every two- and three-drop on the other side while leaving your Dragons untouched, and then gives you four mana that can only be spent on Dragon spells — with five mana in play that is Smaug, Wicked Worm for one black.

title: Molten Mint
text:
The combo turn

Bank the hoard. Four Treasures is the threshold that The Misty Mountains Cold trades in for a 6/6 flying Dragon, and it is also roughly the point where Smaug’s attack trigger halves life totals.
Deploy Smaug the Magnificent. Four mana, or two if Radagast of Rhosgobel discounted him, and he can come down at end of turn thanks to Radagast’s flash clause.
Attack. Smaug deals damage equal to your Treasure count to any target — the opponent, a planeswalker, or the one blocker that matters — and his 4 combat damage rides on top. The upkeep trigger already added a Treasure, so each swing is one point bigger than the last.
Let the swing repeat. Four Treasures is 8 to the face, six is 10, eight is 12. A typical kill line is turn four Smaug attack for 8, upkeep Treasure, turn five attack for 10.

title: Molten Mint
text:
Win condition 2
The second win does not need Smaug. The Misty Mountains Cold’s 6/6 flying Dragon token plus Rapacious Dragon and Flamekin Gildweaver is a legitimate flying clock in a deck that clears the ground with Desolation of Smaug. Last Light of Durin’s Day is the shortcut: fourteen red sources means six quest counters arrive quickly, and the payoff is any Dragon from hand or library directly onto the battlefield. Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant joins the beatdown on his own once Dragons are entering, adding a +1/+1 counter and becoming a flying Dragon each turn.

title: Molten Mint
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep hands with two to three lands and any two-drop that touches the hoard (Gold Pan, Piggy Bank, Bejeweled Warg, Sarkhan, Last Light of Durin’s Day). The best openers are two lands, a two-drop and a three-drop. Ship one-land hands and hands with five or more lands and no engine. Because black and green are splashes, a hand of Mountains plus Treasure makers is keepable — Treasure tokens cast Smaug, Wicked Worm and Radagast without a single Swamp or Forest.

title: Molten Mint
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Smaug the Magnificent counts Treasures at the moment his attack trigger resolves, not when he attacks. Do not crack a Treasure for Stir Up Trouble’s cost before combat if you intend to attack with him.
The Misty Mountains Cold checks for four or more Treasures after every chapter, so with Dori, Plundering Pirate and a Gold Pan already banked it can pop its Dragon as early as chapter two.
Last Light of Durin’s Day counts Mountains entering, not lands. The Lonely Mountain is a Mountain; Swamp and Forest are not. Search Mountains specifically when racing the six counters.
Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant’s behold is a choice: reveal a Dragon card from hand or pick a Dragon you control, then create a Treasure. His second ability triggers on every Dragon that enters, including the 6/6 token from The Misty Mountains Cold and the creature fetched by Last Light of Durin’s Day.
Smaug, Wicked Worm’s treasure burst counts artifacts the opponent controls, so it is weak against creature decks and enormous against Equipment and artifact lists. Its draw trigger fires whenever Treasure mana was spent on the spell, which includes spells paid for by the Treasures it just made.
The Sackville-Bagginses triggers on any token you sacrifice, not just creatures — cracking a Treasure for mana drains the opponent for 1. That makes the ping a real clock when you are chaining Dragons.
The Lonely Mountain enters tapped unless you control an Equipment, and Gold Pan is the only Equipment in the list. Curving Gold Pan into The Lonely Mountain gives you an untapped Mountain that also arms the Dwarf-token ability at one mana off.
Radagast of Rhosgobel discounts only the first creature spell each turn, so sequence a cheap creature first only if you do not want the discount on a Dragon. The discounted spell also gains flash.
Desolation of Smaug’s four mana can only be spent on Dragon spells. Smaug the Magnificent, Smaug, Wicked Worm and Rapacious Dragon are the only legal uses in this list.
Stir Up Trouble’s additional cost is an artifact or creature or four generic mana. Piggy Bank is the ideal sacrifice, because it turns into a Treasure on the way out.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
Game plan in three phases

Build the coin engine (turns 1-3). Land Ambitious Augmenter, Magda, the Hoardmaster, Discerning Financier, or Goldvein Hydra on two. Discerning Financier is the most reliable Treasure in the deck because an opponent almost always has more lands than a five-color deck on turn three. Seize the Spoils and Redcap Thief keep the coin flowing while digging for the counter creatures.
Turn coin into cards and counters (turns 3-5). Resolve Pensive Professor, Berta, Wise Extrapolator, and Topiary Lecturer. From here every spell is a cantrip off the Professor, and every Treasure cracked is a Void trigger. Hold mana up: cracking Treasure is an instant-speed action, so you can make Void live during your own combat step.
Convert (turns 5+). Grow a Fractal with Berta, or land Fractal Tender for a free 3/3 Fractal every end step, then clear a path with Rogue's Passage. If the board stalls, attack with Alpharael instead — half of a life total does not care about blockers.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
Curve and mana
Eighteen of the thirty-six nonland cards cost three, which is exactly what Increment wants: three mana beats the power or toughness of a 1/1, a 2/2, a 0/2, and a 0/3, so the entire counter suite grows off a normal curve. The deck does not need to reach five mana to function — five-drops are three cards, all of them finishers.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
Early game
Lead with lands and a two-drop. Magda, the Hoardmaster and Discerning Financier are the best turn-two plays because they generate coin without asking anything of you. Do not crack Treasure just because you can — hold it until either you need the mana for a spell that increments something, or you need Void live in the same turn you attack with Alpharael or end the turn with Elegy Acolyte.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
Mid game
The priority order is Pensive Professor, then Berta, then everything else. A resolved Professor turns Seize the Spoils into draw three and turns every future spell into a cantrip; it is the card that wins long games. Berta is the answer to color screw: she taps for one mana of any color per counter, and since she increments on any two-mana spell she usually offers two or three colors by turn six.
Topiary Lecturer is the quiet ramp piece. It is a 1/2, so it increments off three-mana spells, and it taps for green equal to its power — a Lecturer that has grown twice is a three-mana land that also attacks.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
The combo turn
The deck’s “combo” is a loop rather than a single turn:

Have Pensive Professor or Berta and at least two Treasures.
Cast a three-mana spell using Treasure mana. Increment triggers, Professor draws you a card, and two Treasures have left the battlefield, so Void is live.
At end of turn, Elegy Acolyte makes a Robot and Insatiable Skittermaw grows. If you have Fractal Tender out and incremented it, you also get a 3/3 Fractal.
Next turn the board is wider, the mana is bigger, and Berta can dump X counters into a Fractal.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
Win condition 2
Alpharael, Stonechosen is a 3/3 with ward, and its Void attack trigger makes the defending player lose half their life, rounded up. Twenty life becomes ten, then five, then three. Because it is life loss and not damage, it ignores blockers, fog effects, and indestructible creatures — the only answer is removing Alpharael or keeping Void offline, and keeping Void offline means never cracking a Treasure, which the deck simply does not do. Cracking a Treasure during your own combat step is the cleanest way to turn the trigger on after blockers are declared.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
Mulligan guide

Keep any hand with two lands, a two-drop, and a three-drop.
Keep one-land hands only with Ambitious Augmenter or Discerning Financier and a second land on top.
Ship hands with no blue and no Treasure: the deck cannot function without a Professor or Berta.
Ship five-land hands with no engine. The deck draws well once it has a Professor, but it has no way to convert raw land into action on its own.

title: Loose Change Leviathan
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Void checks the whole turn, not the stack. A Treasure cracked in your first main phase keeps Void live through combat and the end step, so one coin can pay for a spell, enable Alpharael’s attack trigger, and turn on Elegy Acolyte in the same turn.
Increment counts mana spent, not mana in the cost. Treasure mana, Berta’s any-color mana, and Topiary Lecturer’s green all count. Casting a spell for free does not.
Pensive Professor’s threshold is zero. At 0 power, any spell with at least one mana spent increments her. She never stops drawing.
Berta’s counter trigger is not optional and not once a turn. Two spells that both increment her in one turn means two mana of any color.
Ambitious Augmenter wants to die with counters on it. Attack into a bad block on purpose late in the game: the Fractal arrives with the Augmenter’s counters already on it, which is often a straight upgrade.
Goldvein Hydra is the deck’s best topdeck. Cast it for four or five, it increments the whole team, and when it dies it refunds the mana as Treasures, which then turns Void on for the rest of that turn.
Magda needs a crime. Temporal Intervention targeting an opponent is a crime; so is any removal pointed at their board. The three-Treasure Scorpion Dragon is a real clock against decks that wall the ground.

title: Drydock Overclock

Game plan in three phases

Deploy bodies and the doubler (turns two to four). Two mana threats first — Rot-Curse Rakshasa, Oreplate Pangolin, Sunstar Chaplain — and Loading Zone at the first opportunity, ideally warped in for one green so the four mana never has to be held up. Ship hands with only one coloured source and no Evolving Wilds; five colours is real and the deck cannot afford to be colour-screwed. A hand of Dawnsire plus Drill Too Deep plus Loading Zone is a snap keep even with four lands, because the finish only needs one turn.

title: Drydock Overclock
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Station is sorcery speed only. You cannot station in response to removal, so sequence it in your first main phase before combat, and remember the tapped creature cannot block that turn.
Loading Zone doubles the counters from Systems Override to twenty, but the delayed trigger only removes ten — that is where the permanent ten counters come from.
Loading Zone also doubles +1/+1 counters on your creatures, so Sunstar Chaplain and Oreplate Pangolin grow twice as fast while it is out.
Station can tap a creature that is already a creature-hull: a stationed Sawship at 6/5 can feed six counters (twelve doubled) into the Dreadnought.
Rot-Curse Rakshasa is decayed, so it dies at end of combat if it attacks. Stationing it never triggers decayed, which is usually the better use of a 5/5.
Pugnacious Hammerskull gets a stun counter if it attacks without another Dinosaur, so attack with it once and then park it in a hull.
Kavaron, Memorial World enters tapped; it is a Station land, not a fixing land.

title: Drydock Overclock
text:
Matchups

Fast red aggro: the worst matchup. Lumen-Class Frigate and Rot-Curse Rakshasa are the early blockers; trade, then race in the air with Sawship.
Midrange and control: good. Hulls dodge sorcery-speed creature removal while they are artifacts, Sledge-Class Seedship rebuilds after sweepers, and the Dreadnought’s 100-damage trigger beats a single blocker.
Other combo decks: the deck’s clock is turn six to seven, so it usually wants to be the aggressor; Systems Override can also steal and untap an opposing artifact in a pinch.

Twenty-five lands: three Uncharted Haven, two Branch of Vitu-Ghazi, two Rogue’s Passage, two Terramorphic Expanse, and sixteen basics. text:
Mulligan guide

Keep: two or three lands that include at least one of white, green or black, plus a turn-two face-down body or a two-mana Mount. Five-colour hands without Uncharted Haven or a fetch land are slow even when they have three lands.
Keep: any hand with Pyrotechnic Performer and two disguise creatures. The Performer doubles the value of every body you already planned to play.
Trim: hands of only Saddle 4 payoffs (Seraphic Steed, Guardian Sunmare) with no cheap bodies; hands with fewer than two lands; hands with three different basic lands and no fetch or Haven, which usually means no turn-two play.

title: Veiled Cavalry
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Turning a creature face up is a special action: it does not use the stack, so an opponent cannot kill the creature in response and stop the flip. The Performer trigger happens afterwards and can be responded to, but the damage source is already face up.
A face-down creature has no name and no creature types, so two disguise cards cannot be targeted by effects that name a type, and a face-down card is not a Mount, a Soldier, or anything else. It is still a creature for Saddle, and it is still power 2.
Saddle taps the saddling creatures, and tapped creatures can still be turned face up later (the flip does not tap anything). Dog Walker’s vigilance is the exception that lets one body saddle and attack in the same combat.
Forum Familiar’s flip trigger returns a permanent you control to your hand: use it on a flipped Hunted Bonebrute to re-cast it face down for {3} and flip it again, or on a spent Branch of Vitu-Ghazi, whose flip already produced its mana.
Branch of Vitu-Ghazi stops being a land while it is face down. Count your lands before casting it, and cast it in a turn where a creature is worth more than a colourless land.
Caustic Bronco drains each opponent only when it is saddled; when it is not, you take the life loss instead. Saddle it or do not attack with it.
Hunted Bonebrute gifts the opponent two 1/1 Dogs when it enters face up, which is worth remembering when you are one point short of lethal and the opponent is blocking with them.
Guardian Sunmare finds mana value 3 or less, so it cannot fetch the flipped Crowd-Control Warden (mana value 5). Aim it at Pyrotechnic Performer, Ornery Tumblewagg, Dog Walker, or Concealed Weapon.

title: Redline Alibi
text:
Overview
Two mechanics share one engine. Max speed is a counter that starts at 1 the moment any “Start your engines!” permanent is on the battlefield, increases once on each of your turns when an opponent loses life, and caps at 4. Every card with a “Max speed —” clause switches on permanently once you reach 4, and speed never drops. The problem with most speed decks is that they need combat damage every single turn to climb the ladder.
Suspect solves that problem. A suspected creature has menace and cannot block. Suspecting the creatures you already wanted to attack inverts the drawback (a creature that cannot block is one you were never blocking with) and turns on the part of the deck that outraces a stalled board. J. Jonah Jameson rewards the board state directly: whenever a creature you control with menace attacks, you get a Treasure. Suspected creatures have menace for free, so every suspected attacker is also a Treasure, and Treasures pay for the last points of damage.
The engine is therefore: suspect a board, attack with menace, collect Treasures and life loss, let speed climb, then convert at 4. Speed is charged by damage to opponents from attack triggers that do not care about blockers (Far Fortune, End Boss), from land drops (Jagged Barrens) and from entry pings (Gastal Thrillseeker), so the deck reaches max speed on schedule even when a creature is stonewalled.

title: Redline Alibi
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Lead with whichever one drop is in hand. Burnout Bashtronaut is the best turn one because it is both a “Start your engines!” permanent (speed 1) and a menace body that turns on J. Jonah Jameson later. Frantic Scapegoat is the alternative: it enters already suspected, and from then on every other creature you cast lets you move the suspicion onto the newcomer. That means Scapegoat itself stops being suspected and can block, while the new creature becomes the menace attacker. Keep that loop in mind before combat.
Turn two or three, Gastal Thrillseeker is the cleanest climb: it deals 1 damage to an opponent on entry, which is a life loss event, so speed increases that turn without attacking into a bad block. Momentum Breaker and Kickoff Celebrations do the same job while trading for a card or an opposing creature: Kickoff Celebrations filters your draw, Momentum Breaker makes each opponent sacrifice a creature or a Vehicle, and punishes anyone who cannot by making them discard.


The combo turn
The turn you want is one where speed reaches 4 with a board already in place. The reliable line on turn 4 is Far Fortune, End Boss: whenever you attack, it deals 1 damage to each opponent, so the attack step itself charges speed, and because the damage goes to every opponent rather than to blockers, a stalled board does not stop the counter. Max speed then applies from that point on: Far Fortune adds 1 to every damage source you control (Outpace Oblivion’s 2 becomes 3, Gastal Thrillseeker’s entry ping becomes 2, combat damage gets strictly better), Burnout Bashtronaut gains double strike, Gastal Thrillseeker gains deathtouch and haste, and Hazoret becomes a legal attacker.
From there the kill is usually blunt: suspect everything, attack with menace so single blockers are illegal blocks, bank Treasures from J. Jonah Jameson, and use Rogue’s Passage or Hazoret’s {1}, {T} ability on a power 2 or less creature to make the final attacker unblockable. Burnout Bashtronaut at max speed with {2} of pump and Far Fortune’s bonus attacks as a 2/1 double striker that deals 4, and any blocker trading with Gastal Thrillseeker dies to deathtouch.


Win condition 2: burn that does not need the red zone
Outpace Oblivion is a removal spell first (5 damage to a creature or planeswalker on entry, 6 with Far Fortune online) and a finisher second: {2}, sacrifice it and it deals 2 damage to each player who does not have max speed, which is every opponent in practice, 3 with Far Fortune. Two of them plus Gastal Thrillseeker pings and a Restless Vents attack close games where the ground is locked. Generous Plunderer adds a second non-combat axis: its attack trigger deals damage to the defending player equal to the number of artifacts they control, and its upkeep trigger hands them a Treasure, so the damage grows every turn you keep it alive.


Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two or three lands and at least one one-drop, especially Burnout Bashtronaut or Frantic Scapegoat. Keep a hand with a Jagged Barrens or Gastal Thrillseeker because it guarantees the first speed increase on schedule. Send back four or more land hands without action, hands with no “Start your engines!” permanent, and hands that are all three and four drops, because speed starts only when a permanent is on the battlefield and this deck needs to be charging from turn one.


Key interactions and edge cases

Suspected creatures cannot block. Frantic Scapegoat’s transfer ability is the fix: cast a creature, hand the suspicion to the newcomer, and Scapegoat is free to block again.
J. Jonah Jameson can suspect an opposing creature. A suspected blocker has menace and cannot block, so it can be used as tempo before your attack.
Presumed Dead on Gastal Thrillseeker is a two-for-one in disguise: the creature dies, returns already suspected, and the entry ping fires again for another damage and another speed increase.
Rune-Brand Juggler sacrifices a suspected creature (a suspect that has done its job, a Treasure is not a creature, so use a redundant body) to give an opposing creature -5/-5, which kills anything with 5 toughness or less and is not damage, so it beats indestructible.
Betrayer’s Bargain can be paid with a spent enchantment instead of mana: Momentum Breaker and Kickoff Celebrations have already done their entry work by the time you want the 5 damage.
Barbed Servitor is indestructible and suspects itself, so it is a permanent menace attacker that draws a card on combat damage, and any damage dealt to it makes a target opponent lose that much life, which charges speed.
Max speed is permanent. Once you touch 4, every “Max speed —” clause on the battlefield is on for the rest of the game, including the ones on cards you have not drawn yet.
Restless Vents animating does not use a creature slot, and it triggers J. Jonah Jameson because it has menace when it attacks as an Insect.



Matchups

Against aggro: you have the better race. Momentum Breaker makes them sacrifice a creature, Gastal Thrillseeker gains you 1 and blocks as a 2/3, and Betrayer’s Bargain is efficient removal. Suspected creatures cannot block, so do not over-extend into their attack; keep Frantic Scapegoat unsuspected where possible.
Against control: speed climbing does not require connecting, thanks to Far Fortune and Gastal Thrillseeker, so wipes are survivable. Presumed Dead returns a dead attacker already suspected, Clandestine Meddler surveils every suspect attack, and Barbed Servitor draws. Hold Rogue’s Passage for the turn after their board wipe.
Against midrange: suspected attackers with menace force double blocks, which trades badly against deathtouch and double strike at max speed. Outpace Oblivion answers a single large blocker and then converts into reach.
Against decks with no creatures: the burn axis carries. Two Outpace Oblivion activations plus Plunderer and Thrillseeker pings is 10 or more damage without a single attacker connecting.

Case of the Gorgon’s Kiss counts creature cards put into graveyards from anywhere this turn — evoke deaths, combat deaths, and Case of the Crimson Pulse’s discard all count; tokens do not.
Case of the Burning Masks needs three different sources you controlled to deal damage — one Boltwave is one source, Warleader’s Call pings are one source (no matter how many times it pings), and each attacking creature is its own source.
Case of the Crimson Pulse solves at the beginning of your end step if your hand is empty — cast or evoke everything in the second main phase, then loot into a fresh grip on the next upkeep.
Suspected creatures have menace and can’t block — the Skeleton attacks but never blocks; do not hold it back expecting defense.
Firebending mana from Cruel Administrator’s Soldiers and Fire Nation Palace lasts until end of combat — spend it on instants like Torch the Tower or on the Burning Masks exile chain during or after combat.

title: Weaving Suspicion
text:
Curve and mana
The deck curves 10 / 13 / 13 across one through three mana with nothing above three, an average nonland cost of 2.08. That flat curve is deliberate: Eerie triggers want enchantments to keep arriving, and the cheapest enchantments (Convenient Target, Case of the Stashed Skeleton, Demonic Ruckus, Impact Tremors, Sheltered by Ghosts) are exactly the cost range where you can cast a threat and an enchantment in the same turn.
Twenty-four lands support four colours. Hallowed Fountain and Shadowy Backstreet are the two true duals, Spirebluff Canal and Gloomlake Verge carry the red and black requirements, Mystic Monastery fixes the three-colour Arachne, and the two Restless manlands double as win conditions. Roughly fourteen white, twelve blue, eight black and eight red sources are enough because the deck is white and blue at heart, with red as the enchantment colour and black as the drain colour. Six of the twenty-four lands enter tapped, so keep two-land hands only when one of the two is an untapped source.

title: Weaving Suspicion
text:
Early game
Turn one is Optimistic Scavenger or Frantic Scapegoat, and turn two is an enchantment. Convenient Target is the ideal two-spell start: it costs a single red, it turns the Scavenger into a 2/2 menace attacker, and it fires the Scavenger’s Eerie trigger for a third counter. Case of the Stashed Skeleton does the same job a turn slower but leaves a 2/1 menace token that keeps attacking after the Case has solved itself.
Do not be afraid to attack with everything suspected. Suspected creatures cannot block, so they are dead weight on defence regardless; converting them into damage, Jameson Treasures and meddler surveils is always better than holding them back.

title: Weaving Suspicion
text:
Mid game
Once Gremlin Tamer or Balemurk Leech lands, the deck stops being a pure aggro deck. Every enchantment you play from here is a token plus a point of drain, and Entity Tracker turns the same trigger into a card. The correct line is usually to lead with the cheapest enchantment each turn, let the Eerie triggers resolve, then attack with the menaced team. J. Jonah Jameson should be deployed before a big attack so that each menace attacker pays you a Treasure.

title: Weaving Suspicion
text:
The engine turn
The deck’s best turn is a chain rather than a single play. With a payoff or two in play, cast the enchantment you held from last turn: Convenient Target (suspect plus Eerie), followed by Demonic Ruckus on the same creature (menace plus trample plus Eerie), then attack with the menaced team for Jameson Treasures and meddler surveils. Because Demonic Ruckus draws when it dies and Convenient Target returns from the graveyard, a single removal spell does not break the loop. Entity Tracker held up as an instant lets you run the same line on the opponent’s turn.

title: Weaving Suspicion
text:
Win condition 2: the drain
The deck does not have to win through combat. Balemurk Leech drains one life per enchantment entry, Gremlin Tamer and Case of the Stashed Skeleton add bodies that Impact Tremors converts into damage, and Victor, Valgavoth’s Seneschal grinds the opponent’s hand and graveyard while you do it. When the board is stalled by a bigger defence, stop attacking into it, keep cycling enchantments through Convenient Target’s graveyard recursion, and let the drain and the manlands finish the game.

title: Weaving Suspicion
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep two or three lands when the hand has a one-drop and an enchantment; a two-lander with Optimistic Scavenger plus two enchantments is a keep because the deck’s curve stops at three. A hand of only three-drops should be mulliganed: the deck needs a turn-one or turn-two play to make the Eerie engine function. Always keep a hand with an untapped white or blue source and one of the two-mana payoffs.

title: Weaving Suspicion
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Eerie fires on any enchantment entering, including Auras cast onto creatures you already control, so a pump spell is also a drain trigger and a card.
Convenient Target recurs from the graveyard for {2}{R}, which means the deck has a repeatable Eerie enabler every turn once a Treasure or a land spare is available.
Case of the Stashed Skeleton solves as soon as you control no suspected Skeletons; attacking the 2/1 into a trade, or simply letting Frantic Scapegoat move the suspicion elsewhere, solves it and unlocks the tutor.
Frantic Scapegoat moves suspicion from itself to another creature whenever a creature enters, so it can re-arm a Jameson attack or free a blocker at instant-relevant timing on your own turn.
Web-slinging returns a tapped creature to hand, not a land: bounce a spent suspected attacker, not a blocker you might need. Suspected creatures cannot block anyway, which makes them the natural fodder.
Arachne, Psionic Weaver names a card type when it enters and taxes it; against a deck that leans on one card type, keep it, but do not agonise over the choice.
Suspected creatures have menace and cannot block. If the opponent races, remember that the whole team is offence only; Sheltered by Ghosts and the lifelink it grants are the best way to stabilise.

title: Saddle, Sift, Surge
text:
Early game
Turn one is Dark Matter Manipulator when you have it: three cards in the graveyard immediately, and a 1/2 that grows into a real attacker once the yard crosses seven and fourteen. Turn two is White Tiger, Seraphic Steed or Stubborn Burrowfiend. Do not run the Burrowfiend out without a plan to saddle it on turn three, because its mill only happens when it becomes saddled.
Saddling is the cost the deck is built to cheat. Stubborn Burrowfiend and Ornery Tumblewagg both want only two power, so a two-drop plus any token or one-drop pays it. Seraphic Steed and Guardian Sunmare want four, which is why the Angel tokens from the Steed matter: one Angel plus a two-drop saddles the Sunmare every turn afterwards.

title: Saddle, Sift, Surge
text:
Mid game
Guardian Sunmare changes the texture of the deck. From the turn it lands, every combat does three things at once: it puts a permanent onto the battlefield for free, it triggers that permanent’s power-up at a discount because the permanent entered this turn, and it grows your board without spending a card. Fetch in this order:

White Tiger, Ava Ayala when you need a body that cannot be chump blocked forever.
Bold Biochemist when your hand is empty and you need the two cards.
Stubborn Burrowfiend when the graveyard is already deep and you want the biggest possible attacker.
Guidelight Matrix when you have no way to saddle the following turn.

Alacrian Armory is the second half of that plan. At the beginning of combat it saddles a Mount outright, so a Sunmare, Steed or Burrowfiend attack costs you zero creatures tapped. Every spare copy of Guidelight Matrix does the same job for {2} at sorcery speed.

title: Saddle, Sift, Surge
text:
The combo turn
The turn that usually ends the game:

Start combat with Ornery Tumblewagg plus one other creature and a Mount that can be saddled.
Tumblewagg’s beginning-of-combat trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on your best attacker, usually the Sunmare or a Burrowfiend.
Saddle Tumblewagg (two power) and attack. Its saddled trigger doubles the counters on that creature.
Sunmare attacks saddled as well, putting White Tiger onto the battlefield, then the postcombat main pays {4} for her power-up for a counter and The Tiger God.
Activate Rogue’s Passage on whichever creature now has the most counters. Doubling counters plus an unblockable attacker is usually lethal two turns after the first doubling, and the pattern is 1, 4, 10, 22 counters if you keep doubling the same body.

Blossoming Tortoise makes Rogue’s Passage cost three instead of four, which is often the difference between doubling and connecting in the same turn.

title: Saddle, Sift, Surge
text:
Win condition 2
The mill kill does not care about blockers. Riverchurn Monument mills two to any target for {1} and a tap, and its exhaust ability makes a player mill cards equal to the number of cards in their own graveyard. The Water Crystal makes every opposing mill four cards larger. Sequence:

Chip the opponent with Monument activations and any Dark Matter Manipulator mills while you build a board. Twenty cards in their graveyard is the target.
Land The Water Crystal, then exhaust the first Monument: they mill twenty four, going to forty four.
Exhaust the second Monument: they mill forty eight. Any library under ninety two cards is gone.

Against decks that gain life or wall up the ground, this is the plan that actually closes, and it costs two cards plus a Monument you were already tapping.

title: Saddle, Sift, Surge
text:
Mulligan guide

Keep: one or two green sources, a one-drop or two-drop creature, and ideally Run Over or Alacrian Armory to interact.
Keep: Dark Matter Manipulator plus Stubborn Burrowfiend, the fastest mill start in the deck.
Keep: Guardian Sunmare hands with three lands and any two-drop, since Sunmare repays the whole curve on its own.
Throw back: hands with no green source, hands with only Island and Swamp, and hands that need both Sunmare and Water Crystal to function.
Throw back: one-land hands even with a Manipulator, because the deck cannot afford to miss its third land drop with four colors in the list.

title: Saddle, Sift, Surge
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Power-up discount is evaluated when you activate, not when the creature entered. Guardian Sunmare puts a creature in during combat, so its power-up is still discounted in your second main phase that same turn.
Saddle only as a sorcery. Alacrian Armory and Guidelight Matrix get around that by making a Mount saddled at the beginning of combat, which is also why they let you attack with every creature instead of tapping saddlers.
Stubborn Burrowfiend’s mill triggers only the first time it becomes saddled each turn, so saddling it twice in a turn does nothing extra.
Power-up abilities can be activated once per creature, but a creature that leaves and returns is a new object. Unliving Legionnaire’s power-up returns a creature to hand, and replaying it re-arms its own power-up.
Hedge Shredder puts milled lands onto the battlefield tapped. With Blossoming Tortoise out, milling becomes ramp, and the Tortoise’s “activated abilities of lands cost {1} less” reduces Rogue’s Passage and Restless Cottage activation costs.
The Water Crystal only adds four when an opponent would mill. Your own self-mill from Burrowfiend, Tortoise and Shredder is unaffected.
Riverchurn Monument’s exhaust counts the graveyard at the moment it resolves, so activate it after combat, not before, once you have added anything to their yard.
Restless Cottage enters tapped. Do not count it as a green source on turn one.

Key interactions and edge cases

Cloak is not the same as disguise. Expose the Culprit re-cloaks face-up disguise creatures, and a cloaked card turns face up for its mana cost rather than its disguise cost. That is a turn-up event, so Pyrotechnic Performer triggers and the creature’s own flip ability repeats.

Valiant fires only the first time each turn. Order your enablers deliberately: Ferocification at the beginning of combat, then the equip, then a spell, so each Valiant creature gets exactly one meaningful target and the counters land where the attack is going.
Emberheart Challenger’s Valiant trigger exiles a card you may play this turn. A creature card exiled this way can still be cast face down for three mana, so the impulse draw feeds the disguise plan.
Whiskervale Forerunner’s Valiant trigger works at instant speed on your turn only for the battlefield clause; if it is not your turn the creature goes to hand instead, which is still a fine way to draw past lands.
Face-down 2/2s with ward 2 make cheap removal and targeted discard awkward. Do not flip early just because you can: hold the mana and the information.
Crowd-Control Warden’s counters are counted on entry or flip, so flip it after the Dogs from Dog Walker are already on the battlefield.

title: The Rewritten Stampede
text:
Overview
The Rewritten Stampede fuses three mechanics into one engine: Saddle mounts attack for value, Convoke spells are cast by tapping the same creatures, and Plan enchantments count every tap. The heart of the deck is Rewrite History: whenever one or more creatures you control become tapped, you draw a card, discard a card, and advance the plan. Attacking, saddling, convoking, and even Station all tap creatures — so every axis of the deck draws cards.
The other two Plans turn the same actions into resources. Death to Our Enemies makes a Treasure for every noncreature spell you cast (all your Convoke spells), which ramps the deck into its 5-6 mana finishers, and caps at 7 damage. Political Triumph turns every creature that enters into scry 1 plus a plan counter, ending in a global +1/+1 anthem.
The payoff is a go-wide Mount army. Seraphic Steed mints 3/3 flying Angels each saddled attack, Bridled Bighorn adds Sheep, Bounding Felidar pumps the whole team, Drover Grizzly gives trample, and Collective Inferno doubles all damage dealt by Mounts. Dracosaur Auxiliary swings in the air with haste and shocks anything. Games end in one massive, doubled, trampling stampede — or a 7-point burn finish.

title: The Rewritten Stampede
text:
Approach

Game plan phases

Setup (T1-3): Play Political Triumph or a cheap Mount (Gilded Ghoda, Seraphic Steed). Untap the Roads lands with a Mount in play and land Rewrite History.
Engine (T3-5): Resolve Rewrite History and Death to Our Enemies. Every saddle tap draws a card; every Convoke spell makes a Treasure. Mounts attack while saddled to generate tokens and Treasures.
Stampede (T5-7): Slam Collective Inferno (choose Mount), saddle Dracosaur Auxiliary / Bounding Felidar / Guardian Sunmare with Pilots and tokens, and attack for doubled, trampling, lifelink damage.
Cleanup: Burn with Death to Our Enemies (7 split), or bury the opponent in cards with Harmonized Crescendo (draw per Mount) and Rewrite History recursion.

The deck runs 23 lands but plays like 26: Treasures from Gilded Ghoda and Death to Our Enemies, plus creature-tapping for Convoke, generate the extra mana.

title: The Rewritten Stampede
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Mulligan for Rewrite History plus any 1-2 drop Mount or Political Triumph. A turn-1 Political Triumph followed by creatures scries every draw step. Gilded Ghoda is the best early Mount: 2/2, saddle 1, and every saddled attack makes a Treasure — ramp and card draw on one body. Seraphic Steed (2/2 first strike, lifelink) races aggro while it waits for saddle 4.


Mid game
Land Death to Our Enemies and start casting Convoke spells — each one makes a Treasure. Unswerving Sloth is the engine-breaker: saddle it (tap 4 power), attack, and it untaps every creature you control, setting up a free main-phase Convoke turn. Guardian Sunmare tutors any nonland permanent with mana value 3 or less on a saddled attack — fetch a second copy of a Plan, another Mount, or a Convoke spell.


The combo turn

Have a wide board of Mounts and at least Collective Inferno (Mount).
Main phase 1: tap Pilots and tokens to saddle Dracosaur Auxiliary (saddle 3), Bounding Felidar (saddle 2) and Guardian Sunmare (saddle 4). Every tap draws a card off Rewrite History and every noncreature spell cast so far made a Treasure.
Attack: Dracosaur flies over for 4 (8 with Inferno) plus 2-4 shock damage; Felidar puts a +1/+1 counter on every other creature and gains life; Drover Grizzly grants trample; Seraphic Steed mints 3/3 Angels; lifelink keeps you ahead.
Main phase 2: Harmonized Crescendo (choose Mount) draws a card per Mount permanent — routinely 8-12 cards — or Unexpected Assistance digs deeper. Rewrite History then returns the best instants/sorceries from the graveyard to hand for the next loop.

A fully developed board deals 25-40 doubled, trampling damage in one swing.


Win condition 2: burn and grind
Death to Our Enemies reaches four plan counters after four noncreature spells (Plans, Convoke spells, and lands’ activated abilities do not count — spells only). That is easy with this shell: the payoff is 7 damage split as you choose, usually 7 to the face to finish after one stampede. In grindy games, Rewrite History recurs Temporal Cleansing, Appeal to Eirdu, and Unexpected Assistance, while Harmonized Crescendo refills the hand off the Mount count.


Mulligan guide
Keep: any hand with Rewrite History or Political Triumph plus 2-3 lands and a creature. Keep 2-land hands only with a 1-2 drop Mount (Gilded Ghoda, Seraphic Steed). Ship: hands without a Mount or a Plan, and hands flooded with 5-6 mana spells. Bucolic Ranch is a strong keep — it fixes and finds the finishers.


Key interactions and edge cases

Rewrite History triggers on any tap: attacking, saddling, convoking, and Station taps all draw. Plan the order — saddle first, then convoke, so each tap draws.
Pilots saddle as power 3: one Pilot covers saddle 1-3; two Pilots cover saddle 4 (Seraphic Steed, Guardian Sunmare, Unswerving Sloth).
The Wandering Rescuer protects tapped creatures with hexproof and blocks with flash, double strike — cast it with Convoke at instant speed.
Temporal Cleansing answers anything nonland, including indestructible threats (it tucks instead of destroying).
Adagia copies an enchantment at 12+ charge counters: copying Collective Inferno quadruples Mount damage; copying a Plan re-runs its payoff.
Death to Our Enemies cares about spells, not abilities: saddling and Station do not advance it, Convoke spells and Plans do.



Matchups

Aggro: Seraphic Steed’s lifelink, The Wandering Rescuer’s flash blocks, and Bounding Felidar’s lifegain stabilize; stall until the stampede.
Control: Death to Our Enemies ramps you through counterspells (Treasures are instant-speed mana), Rewrite History restocks after board wipes, and hexproof from The Wandering Rescuer protects tapped attackers.
Midrange: out-muscle with Angels, trample, and doubled damage; Temporal Cleansing removes the single biggest blocker.

title: Hoardwyrm
text:
Curve and mana
The deck curves 5 / 13 / 9 / 3 / 2 / 4 across two through seven mana with an average nonland mana value of 3.89, and the Treasure tokens pay the top of that curve early. Counting lands, the base offers roughly fifteen red sources, nine black and nine green, with Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon adding any colour for Dragon spells. Red is the deepest because Smaug the Magnificent wants {R}{R} and Desert Were-Worm and Stone-Giant of High Pass both cost {R}{R} as well; black is only needed for Smaug, Wicked Worm’s {B} and My Precious’ adventure.
Twenty-four lands is deliberate. The deck has no one-mana accelerant, so hitting land three on time matters, and the Treasure makers want a fourth land before the top end arrives. The probability of four lands by turn four is 0.635, and the deck’s goldfish turn-4 consistency is 0.629. The Lonely Mountain enters tapped unless you control an Equipment, so curve it behind Orcrist, My Precious or Getaway Barrel rather than leading with it.

title: Hoardwyrm
text:
Early game
Turns one and two are about the cheapest possible board. Bejeweled Warg is the best turn-two play: a 3/2 trampler that turns any connection into either a Treasure or a +1/+1 counter on a Wolf, which means it is never a wasted card in a hand that lacks a Dragon. Against an aggressive opponent, hold Last Light of Durin’s Day as a two-mana enchantment that will eventually hand you a free Dragon, and remember that its Mountaincycling lets you trade it for a land when the board does not want it.

title: Hoardwyrm
text:
Mid game
Turn three is the pivot. Dori, Bearer of Friends is the deck’s cleanest use of three mana: the 3/2 trampler adds a Treasure the moment it lands, which is one mana toward the next Dragon and one more count for Smaug. The Misty Mountains Cold wants to be cast in the same window, because every chapter adds a Treasure and the saga converts to a 6/6 flying Dragon the moment the count reaches four.
Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane is the deck’s value glue. He triggers on every noncreature spell, which in this deck means the two sagas, every Equipment, Getaway Barrel and the Spew Flame adventure, so each of those cards drains each opponent for 1 and grows Gandalf by +1/+1. Sequence him before the sagas and the Equipment rather than after.

title: Hoardwyrm
text:
The combo turn
The killing turn is a chain of Treasure events that all point at one number:

Smaug the Magnificent is on the battlefield with a hoard already banked.
Attack. Smaug’s trigger deals damage equal to the number of Treasures you control to any target, and the attack itself is a 4/3 flier the opponent must answer.
If the count is still short, cash The Misty Mountains Cold’s fourth chapter: four Treasures become a 6/6 flying Dragon token that attacks from that point on.
Sacrifice the spare artifacts. Stone-Giant of High Pass eats an artifact token for four damage to any target, and Getaway Barrel turns a spent artifact into a free creature.

A representative turn with six mana, Smaug the Magnificent in play and three Treasures: attack for four in the air plus three damage to any target, cast The Misty Mountains Cold and make the fourth Treasure in the same turn to flip the saga into a 6/6 Dragon. The opponent is now facing five power in the air with a Dragon token arriving behind it.

title: Hoardwyrm
text:
Win condition 2
When the burn plan is too slow, the deck switches to mass. Desert Were-Worm punishes a wide board: it gains +2/+0 for every Mountain you control and, the first time each turn you attack with twelve or more total power, untaps every attacker and grants an additional combat phase. With seven Mountains it is a 14/5 that turns a five-creature board into two full attacks.
The alternative clock is Artifact bodies. Stone-Giant of High Pass is a 7/7 that adds a 3/1 Wall on entry and on every attack, Stone Boulder tokens are artifacts that can be sacrificed to the Giant’s own ability, and The Arkenstone turns the whole team into bigger creatures while drawing a card each end step. Orcrist, Goblin-cleaver on any attacker turns a combat step into one Treasure per creature of the chosen type you control, which funds the next Dragon.

title: Hoardwyrm
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep two or three lands if the hand has a turn-two play plus one card that banks Treasures. Hands with Bejeweled Warg and a three-drop, or Dori, Bearer of Friends and The Misty Mountains Cold, are ideal, and any hand containing Smaug the Magnificent with two lands of different colours is a keep — the Dragon is the payoff and the rest of the hand only has to be playable. Ship hands whose only lands enter tapped and that lack a two-mana play, because the deck cannot afford to fall a full turn behind on board, and ship one-land hands even with a perfect curve of Dragons.

title: Hoardwyrm
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Smaug the Magnificent counts Treasures on the attack trigger, so hold Treasure cracking until after attackers are declared — the damage is dealt before you need the mana.
The upkeep Treasure from Smaug the Magnificent arrives before your draw step, so it is available to cast a spell that same turn.
Smaug, Wicked Worm creates Treasures equal to the opponent’s artifact count, which can be zero: against an artifact-light deck treat it as a 5/5 flier with a Treasure-to-draw converter and not as a ramp spell.
The Misty Mountains Cold checks four Treasures on every chapter, not only on the fourth: if you already control four when the second chapter resolves, the saga immediately converts into the 6/6 Dragon.
Treasure tokens sacrifice for any colour, so they fix the deck’s black and green costs as well as its red ones.
Smaug the Magnificent, Desert Were-Worm, Stone-Giant of High Pass and Smaug, the Great Calamity all want {R}{R}: do not keep a hand that can only make one red.
Last Light of Durin’s Day needs six quest counters, and only Mountains add counters. Five basic Mountains and two The Lonely Mountain are the seven Mountain cards in the deck.
Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon’s own mana is restricted to Dragon and Omen spells; use it for Smaug, not for Dori.
Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon’s {4} activation sacrifices the land: use it when you already have six other lands, and search for the Dragon you actually need rather than the biggest one.
Orcrist, Goblin-cleaver makes one Treasure per creature of the chosen type, so choose the type the board actually has — Dragon is the biggest number once Smaug and friends are out.
Getaway Barrel triggers when it dies, so sacrifice it to Stone-Giant of High Pass or Allure of Power rather than letting it sit.
Bejeweled Warg’s trigger is a choice on each connection: take the Treasure when you are short of mana or one step from four, and the counter when you need a bigger Wolf.
The Arkenstone is an artifact that anthems the whole team; its Seek the Heart adventure should be cast first when you need to find a legendary creature, then the artifact can follow from exile.
My Precious grants hexproof, not indestructible: it stops targeted removal, not a sweeper.
Burn, Burn, Tree and Fern’s third and fourth chapters add red mana, which is one more way to pay for Smaug without tapping a land.
