Mid game
Turns four through six should be spent casting two or three cheap spells a turn rather than one expensive one. Every noncreature spell is a counter event through Bothersome Noisemaker and a point of damage through Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane, so the turn is counted in triggers: Tidings of War for {R}, Rage into the Valley for {2}{B}, a flashed-back Tidings of War for {3}{R}, and the free amass 2 off Goblin-town’s activation.
Rage into the Valley is the deck’s only natural source of card advantage in the early turns: it draws a card and loses 1 life for {2}{B}, and the Army it amasses is usually the biggest creature on the board from turn four onward. Gathering of Darkness then rebuys whichever Goblin the opponent dealt with, which turns every removal spell they cast into a second counter event.
The Army is the permanent that matters. Keep it in play and keep adding to it; the deck’s damage is delivered in twos, so the attacker does not have to be enormous, only unblockable.

title: Wardrum Warband
text:
The combo turn
The engine turn needs three things on the board: The Great Goblin, Bothersome Noisemaker, and an Army (or any Goblin) to receive the counters.

Start the turn with The Great Goblin and Bothersome Noisemaker in play. Any amassed Army already on the board counts as the Goblin for the counters.
Cast Tidings of War for {R}. Its own amass 1 triggers The Great Goblin for 2, and the Noisemaker’s amass 1 triggers him again for 2. Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane, if he is out, adds 1 more and grows.
Flash back Tidings of War for {3}{R}. Amassing 3 is one event, so it is one trigger for 2 damage, plus the Noisemaker’s 2 — but the Army grows by 4 counters in total and the spell still counts for Gandalf.
Activate Goblin-town: {2}{B}{R}, sacrifice the land, two +1/+1 counters on the Army. That is 2 more damage and a permanent +2/+2.
Sacrifice a Goblin to Bolg’s Company for {B}{R}, then spend it on Rage into the Valley: the sacrifice sets off any death trigger (Fearsome Goblin Pair amasses 4), and the sorcery amasses 2 more and draws a card.

A realistic turn five with both engines in play is 10 to 12 damage that never attacks, on top of a 6/6 or larger Army sitting in play.

title: Wardrum Warband
text:
Win condition 2
The Army wins games that the burn does not. Every amass in the list grows the same token: Flunkies, the Noisemaker, both halves of Tidings of War, Rage into the Valley, Gathering of Darkness, Fearsome Goblin Pair and Goblin-town all feed one creature, and a single Army that has been through three of them is a 7/7 or larger.
My Precious is what makes it lethal. Equipped creature has hexproof and cannot be blocked, and the equip cost is {2} plus 2 life, which is payable every turn. A hexproof unblockable Army is a two-turn clock that ignores most removal and every blocker, and Warg Tactics adds trample and hexproof for a turn on top of it.
Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane is the third, quiet win condition. He grows with every noncreature spell and deals 1 damage to each opponent each time, so a long game of cheap spells and flashback kills a player who has stabilised against the ground attack.

title: Wardrum Warband
text:
Key interactions and edge cases







Interaction
Ruling detail




The Great Goblin counts events, not counters
“Whenever you put one or more counters” is a single trigger no matter how many counters arrive. Amass Goblins 4 from Fearsome Goblin Pair is 2 damage, and so is amass 1 from a Noisemaker — which is why the cheap repeatable amass cards beat the big ones


The Army is a Goblin for every other card
Amass creates the Army as a Goblin, so the counters on it trigger The Great Goblin, Goblin-town can target it, Warg Tactics can put a counter on it and Bolg’s Company can sacrifice it for {B}{R}


Amass creates the 0/0 first, then adds counters
If you control no Army, amass creates a 0/0 black Goblin Army token and then puts the counters on it — still one event, still one burn trigger, and the token survives because the counters arrive with it


The Great Goblin is legendary
A second copy cannot stay on the battlefield. Play the first one and hold the rest as removal-proof re-buys after a sweeper; his second ability does not trigger when he himself dies


Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane triggers on his own adventure
Flameshape is a sorcery while it is on the stack, so casting it is a noncreature spell and triggers the +1/+1 and the 1 damage. The adventured cards are then castable while you control a Wizard, which Gandalf is


Flashback is a noncreature spell
Tidings of War cast from the graveyard for {3}{R} triggers Bothersome Noisemaker for amass 1 and Gandalf for 1 damage, on top of its own amass 3


Bolg’s Company needs another Goblin to have haste
It is a 2/2 that only has haste while you control another Goblin, and its ability requires sacrificing another Goblin — Goblin-town Flunkies, Bothersome Noisemaker, Fearsome Goblin Pair and the Army all qualify


Fearsome Goblin Pair is a 1/1 that dies into a 4-counter amass
The amass happens on death, not on entry, so the pair is a blocker that trades and then feeds the burn. Sacrificing it to Bolg’s Company or to Allure of Power gets both halves of the card


Allure of Power needs a creature to sacrifice
It is an instant for {1}{B} that costs a creature as an additional cost and draws two cards. With no creature on the board it cannot be cast, so keep a spare Goblin in play before you need the cards


Warg Tactics counters a creature you control, including a non-Goblin
The +1/+1 counter only triggers The Great Goblin when the target is a Goblin, Orc or Army. Warg Tactics targets any creature, and putting the counter on Nasty Little Rabbit or Gandalf is a wasted burn trigger


Troll Negotiations fights with the creature that received the counters
The same creature gets two counters and then fights a creature an opponent controls. Cast it on the Army or a Goblin for the burn trigger, and remember that the fight is not optional — do not aim it at something that will die


Goblin-town enters tapped and is sacrificed for its ability
Three copies are in the list because the land is the only card that turns a flooded board into damage. Tapping for {B} or {R} and then sacrificing it for the counters in the same turn is legal as long as you have {2}{B}{R} available


My Precious can be re-equipped every turn
Equip is {2} and 2 life, not a tap, so the Equipment moves between the Army and any blocking Goblin as needed. Hexproof plus unblockable means the opponent must answer the Equipment or the Army itself

title: Balin’s Company

Each Balin trigger: discard your hand (say 5-7 cards), draw that many (doubled by Bard), deal that much to each opponent.

Old Thrush, Bilbo and Capital City make sketchy keepers playable — they filter or fix. Against aggro, prefer basics and untapped lands; the tapped Deserts and Temples are acceptable only with a clean curve behind them.

title: Balin’s Company
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Balin triggers on any Dwarf ETB — including the 2/2 tokens from Fíli, The Lonely Mountain and At the Door. It is “may”: decline if you do not want to shrink your hand.
Bifur doubles Dwarf triggered abilities while Storied — that includes Balin’s burn, Fíli’s token creation, and Nori’s first-strike trigger, but not Belladonna’s (she is a Halfling).
Bard doubles token creation and all draws except the first card of each draw step — Balin’s X-draw and At the Door’s X tokens both double.
Storied is a once-per-game switch: three or more artifacts, legendaries and/or Sagas simultaneously, ever, and the story endures permanently. Restless Anchorage’s Map tokens are artifacts and count.
An Unexpected Party’s adventure must be cast as the sorcery (At the Door) from hand; the enchantment side enters only when cast as the enchantment — pick Dwarf for +2/+2.
The Lonely Mountain enters tapped unless you control an Equipment; this deck runs none, so it always enters tapped — sequence it late in your land drops.
Magnificent End discounts itself by {3} against a tapped creature: pair it with Enchanted River’s Grasp, Gaze in Wonder, or a tapped attacker.
Sound the Trumpets recruits only if the countered spell’s mana value was 2 or less.
Belladonna’s ability resolves in order per turn — the third token each turn pumps the board, so time your token burst for after blockers are declared if needed.
Gandalf’s {6} activation shuffles him into the library — an emergency refill, not a value engine.

title: Balin’s Company

Midrange: Bifur doubles the value of every Dwarf; Belladonna’s draw step keeps the hand full; the combo turn out-damages their board. Use Balin triggers as removal-light burn once they tap out.
Control: Bard, Gandalf and Bilbo refill through counters; At the Door only needs one turn with Balin. Sound the Trumpets fights their sweeper, and Celebrate the Mountain-king exiles their win condition until the kill turn.
Combo race: the Balin burn turn is faster than most engines — prioritize resolving Balin + Bifur over board development, and hold Sound the Trumpets for their enabler.

The alternative clock is Bolg of the North. Sacrificing a high-power creature to its entry trigger deals that much damage to another target creature, and any excess damage converts into amass counters — a one-card removal spell that also grows the main threat. title: Drumbeat Horde

Key interactions and edge cases

Amass always grows the same Army: there is only ever one Army token, so counters from different spells accumulate on the same creature rather than creating multiple bodies.
The Great Goblin counts events, not counters: an amass 4 and an amass 1 each deal 2 damage, they do not scale with the number of counters placed.
Warg Tactics’ counter also triggers The Great Goblin, because the target is a Goblin or an Army — the spell is both protection and another point of drain.
Azog, Moria’s Ruin hands an opposing Army to the opponent whose creature it destroys. Destroy your own expendable creature when you can, or aim at something with power one.
Fearsome Goblin Pair dies on purpose: Stir Up Trouble and Bolg of the North both turn its death into amass 4 plus damage.
Tidings of War is amass 3 when cast from the graveyard through flashback, not amass 1 — the flashback line is the deck’s biggest single counter swing.

Along the Crooked Way’s menace activation is a mana sink for turns when you hold up nothing else, and it applies to the Army as well as your other Goblins.
Goblin-town enters tapped: sequence it on a turn when you do not need the mana, and sacrifice it only at sorcery speed.
Raucous Theater’s surveil fills the graveyard for Gathering of Darkness, so surveilling a creature away is often better than keeping it on top.
The Great Goblin’s death trigger exiles the top card of your library for every Goblin, Orc or Army that dies, so attacking into a bad block is not always wrong — the exchange usually pays you back a card.

title: Firefeeding
text:
Overview
Firefeeding is a five-color engine deck that turns three Standard mechanics into one loop: Warp provides the bodies and the recycling, Firebending pays for them, and Forage converts the leftovers into fuel.
The core insight is that Warp creatures are the cheapest “enters the battlefield” events in the format. Weftstalker Ardent deals 1 damage to each opponent whenever another creature or artifact you control enters, so every warped body, every Food token and every Squirrel is a point of damage to both opponents at once. Warp’s exile clause is not a drawback here: at the beginning of the next end step the warped permanent leaves the battlefield, which switches on every Void card in the deck, and on a later turn you simply cast it again from exile. That second cast gives Fire Lord Zuko two separate triggers (one for casting a spell from exile, one for a permanent entering from exile), putting two +1/+1 counters on every creature you control. Because Zuko’s own firebending is equal to his power, those counters also convert directly into red mana.
Firebending is what makes the mana work. Every firebender that attacks adds that much red mana, usable until end of combat. Since Warp costs are tiny ({R}, {B}, {U}, {1}{W}, {1}{G}), the deck can attack first and then pay for two or three warped spells from combat mana alone. That is also why a five-color basics manabase is viable at all: outside of Fire Lord Zuko and a couple of two-color cards, every colored requirement in the deck is a single pip.
Forage is the third leg. Vinereap Mentor, Camellia, the Seedmiser and Thornvault Forager all turn Food into something more useful: Thornvault Forager forages for two mana of any combination of colors, which is exactly the fixing a five-color deck with basic lands needs; Camellia makes a 1/1 Squirrel whenever you sacrifice a Food, and that Squirrel entering is another Weftstalker trigger; Corpseberry Cultivator forages at the beginning of combat and grows itself in the process. Feed the Cycle uses the same forage clause for removal.

Firebending triggers on the attack, so you float two to four red mana before blockers are even assigned. Blockers cannot take the mana away.
After combat, spend it: a warped Weftstalker Ardent for {R}, a warped Timeline Culler for {B} and 2 life, or a warped Knight Luminary for {1}{W} to make a 1/1 Soldier.
Each of those entries pings each opponent for 1 (Weftstalker Ardent), and each counts as a warped spell, so the end step is live: Voidforged Titan draws you a card, and the warped creatures exile themselves, which is a second “nonland permanent left the battlefield” event for anything that checks it.
Next turn, cast the exiled cards normally. Fire Lord Zuko turns that single cast into two triggers (a spell cast from exile, a permanent entering from exile), so the whole team gets two counters and your firebenders produce more red mana than they did last turn.

Forage slots into any gap in that sequence. Thornvault Forager converts one Food into two mana of any colors, which is how you cast a card in your third or fourth color without the right basic. Camellia, the Seedmiser turns the Food sacrifice into a Squirrel, and Squirrels get menace from her, so the token side of the board is hard to block profitably. Corpseberry Cultivator forages at the beginning of combat and adds a counter each time, which conveniently happens before you attack with it.


Win condition 2 and the finish
Drain alone will not always get there against lifegain, so the deck carries a combat plan. Counters from Fire Lord Zuko and Vindictive Warden’s activated {3} (1 damage to each opponent) keep the pressure on, while Alpharael, Stonechosen ends games outright: with any Void condition live, an Alpharael attack makes the defending player lose half their life, rounded up. Warp a creature, declare the attack, and the condition is satisfied by the warped spell itself.
When the board stalls, Rogue’s Passage breaks it: target the largest firebender (or Alpharael) and the damage is unavoidable. Soulstone Sanctuary does the same job from the other direction by being an attacker that never really leaves.


Mulligan guide







Hand
Action




Two to three lands, a firebender and a Weftstalker or Forager
Keep. This is the deck’s normal opening.


One land, or a hand where every spell needs a second color you do not have
Mulligan. Four lands by turn four is the target, and the manabase is five-color basics, so a greedy hand punishes you.


All lands plus Plasma Bolt
Mulligan past six; the deck needs a body.


No lands but Food and Plasma Bolt
Never keep.





Key interactions and edge cases

Firebending mana lasts until end of combat, so spend it before the combat step ends: cast warped creatures after attackers are declared but before you move to your second main phase, and hold instant-speed forage mana for a Feed the Cycle in the same window.
Warped permanents are exiled at the beginning of the next end step, so they are gone for combat and available to recast on any later turn. This is why the deck never really runs out of cards.
Weftstalker Ardent triggers on any other creature or artifact entering, including Food tokens and the Squirrels from Camellia. Stacking two Weftstalkers doubles the drain on every entry.
Camellia, the Seedmiser’s trigger is on sacrificing one or more Foods, so a single forage that eats one Food makes exactly one Squirrel. Foraging through graveyard exile (three cards) does not make a Squirrel, but it does trigger Corpseberry Cultivator’s counter.
Void checks “a spell was warped this turn” as well as “a nonland permanent left the battlefield”, so you never need to sacrifice anything to switch it on. A single warp in a turn turns on Voidforged Titan, Alpharael, Plasma Bolt and Decode Transmissions at once.
Thornvault Forager’s forage ability exiles three cards from your graveyard if you do not want to spend a Food. Do not strip your graveyard clean if you still want to recast something with Timeline Culler.
Timeline Culler costs {B} and 2 life from the graveyard, which makes it a repeatable drain-adjacent engine with Weftstalker Ardent, at the price of your life total. Do not loop it when you are under pressure.

Never overcommit. Warp cards are perfect here: cast one, let it get exiled, recast it later for free value. Soulstone Sanctuary attacks through sorcery-speed sweepers, and Decode Transmissions refills your hand.

title: Charged Into the Void

Early game
Lead with a one-drop and a two-drop. Deep-Cavern Bat is the strongest turn-two play because it both attacks and removes an answer from the opponent’s hand. Umbral Collar Zealot is the best blocker — three power for two mana means it also puts three charge counters on a Spacecraft when you station with it. title: Charged Into the Void
text:
Mid game
This is where the deck separates from a normal aggro deck. Each turn you want to do two things: leave at least one permanent on the battlefield and then remove or sacrifice a different one. The default line is to station during your precombat main phase (Station is sorcery-speed), then attack, then sacrifice a token or a spent creature in the second main phase so Void is satisfied before the end step.
Key sequencing rule: do your Void-dependent spells in the second main phase, not the first. Plasma Bolt and Tragic Trajectory upgrade only if a nonland permanent has already left the battlefield this turn, so cast your sacrifice effect first and the burn second.

title: Charged Into the Void
text:
The combo turn

Untap with one or more dormant Spacecraft and at least two creatures, one of which you do not need.
Precombat main: choose a Spacecraft and station it repeatedly — each activation taps another creature and adds charge counters equal to its power. Tapping multiple creatures in one turn is legal, because Station has no once-per-turn restriction, only a sorcery-timing restriction.
Check thresholds: 4+ for Wurmwall Sweeper, 6+ for Warmaker Gunship, 3+ for Galvanizing Sawship, 12+ for Lumen-Class Frigate. The moment a Spacecraft hits its threshold it is an artifact creature and can attack.
Attack with the newly created fliers. Sweeper and Gunship fly, Galvanizing Sawship has haste.
Second main: sacrifice a leftover permanent — a Robot token from last turn’s Elegy Acolyte, a Treasure, or a creature to Corrupted Conviction — to keep Void online, and hold Tragic Trajectory or Plasma Bolt to punish any crack-back.

title: Charged Into the Void
text:
Win condition 2: Void attrition
The Robot tokens are the second clock. Elegy Acolyte makes a 2/2 colorless Robot artifact creature token at every end step in which a permanent left the battlefield — and it draws a card whenever your creatures deal combat damage to a player, so it refills your hand while it builds a board. Those Robots then do double duty: they attack, they block, they charge Station (two power each), and they are free sacrifice fodder for Bartolomé or Corrupted Conviction.
Alpharael, Stonechosen is the finisher: when it attacks with Void online, the defending player loses half their life, rounded up. Two attacks — or one attack after burn — ends a game that was never close. Plasma Bolt and Tragic Trajectory also count as reach, and Susur Secundi converts a large creature into cards.

title: Charged Into the Void
text:
Mulligan guide

Keep: two or three lands that cover black plus either white or red, one one-drop, one two-drop, and one sacrifice outlet or Corrupted Conviction.
Keep a one-lander only if it is a Swamp and the hand has Greedy Freebooter plus Umbral Collar Zealot — the curve is low enough to recover.
Ship: hands with no black source, hands with only five- and six-drops, and hands with three or more lands that enter tapped (Adagia and Susur Secundi both enter tapped, so two of them plus no basic is a real cost).
The deck is more resilient than most midrange decks because sacrificing is a feature, not a cost — a hand of interchangeable small creatures plus one outlet is playable.

title: Charged Into the Void
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Station is sorcery-speed only. You cannot charge a Spacecraft in response to removal or during combat. Do it in your main phase before you attack.
Station has no once-per-turn limit. Multiple creatures can be tapped in the same turn to charge one Spacecraft; a single Lumen-Class Frigate tap adds three counters, an Umbral Collar Zealot tap adds three more, and a Warmaker Gunship tap adds four.
Charge counters do not add up across cards. Each Spacecraft tracks its own counters; Adagia and Susur Secundi are Planets with their own 12+ abilities, they are not Spacecraft and never become creatures.
Void checks the whole turn, not the end step. A permanent that left the battlefield during combat still satisfies Void at the end step, so trading creatures in combat is a legitimate way to switch Void on.
Void counts any player’s permanents. When removal or an opponent’s own sacrifice effect makes them lose a permanent, that also turns your Void triggers on — your end-step payoffs only care that something left the battlefield, not whose it was.
Lumen-Class Frigate’s anthem is live at two counters, not twelve. The twelve-counter mode (flying lifelink) is a bonus; the +1/+1 pump is the reason to play it, and it also makes your stationing creatures hit harder next turn.
Sacrificing to Corrupted Conviction is an additional cost. If the spell is countered the creature is still gone, so treat it as a sacrifice outlet with a draw-two rider rather than a protection spell.
Adagia copies artifacts you control, including charged Spacecraft. The copy is legendary, so copying a legendary Spacecraft means you keep only one; copy a non-legendary charged Warmaker Gunship or Galvanizing Sawship instead.

title: Charged Into the Void
text:
Matchups

Aggro: the deck has cheap blockers (Umbral Collar Zealot, Deep-Cavern Bat), lifelink, and a very low curve. Trade early, keep Void switched on so Elegy Acolyte keeps producing Robots, and win the ground fight with Bartolomé growing into a real threat.
Control: play into Void deliberately. Sacrifice tokens to force the payoffs, keep a Wurmwall Sweeper or Galvanizing Sawship back as a threat that only needs three or four counters, and hold Alpharael for a turn where the opponent has tapped out. The deck’s threats are artifacts, so artifact removal is the main concern.
Midrange: the mirror-ish grind — Interceptor Mechan returns your best artifact or creature from the graveyard, so the deck recovers from sweepers better than it looks. Susur Secundi is the long-game engine: sacrifice a big creature to draw four or five cards and refill.
Combo: no counterspells, so the plan is speed and disruption. Deep-Cavern Bat’s exile is the best tool; Tragic Trajectory with Void online kills a combo creature through most protection.

title: Gift Economy
text:
Early game
Turns one and two are for the engine, not for damage. Razorkin Needlehead is the best turn-two play in the deck because it turns every later Gift spell into damage, but Gleaming Splendor is the more important one against anything slow: it starts paying Treasures the moment the opponent’s draw step plus any gift draw makes two cards, and the Treasures are what pay for the three- and five-mana halves of the deck.
Do not cast removal without the gift. Parting Gust without a promise is a temporary exile that gives the creature back with a +1/+1 counter; with the promise it exiles the creature forever, and if Needlehead or Crawler is out the card the opponent draws costs them 1 or 2 life. The same logic applies to Nocturnal Hunger, which only makes us lose 2 life when the Food is not promised, and to Blooming Blast, which loses 3 points of reach without its Treasure.
Sanguine Syphoner is the safest turn-two body: a 1/3 that drains on every attack and survives most one- and two-mana removal. Melancholic Poet, on the other hand, is a 2/2 that should be played on a turn when a Parting Gust, Nocturnal Hunger or Blooming Blast is already in hand, because otherwise it does nothing.

Turn three is when the drain engine starts compounding. Scrawling Crawler draws both players a card in the upkeep, taking 1 life off the opponent, and then any Gift-a-card spell that turn takes another 1 or 2 and hands us a Treasure from Gleaming Splendor. A turn of Crawler, Consumed by Greed with the gift promised and a Melancholic Poet trigger is 4 points of life loss and a creature sacrificed, from three cards.
The board is meant to be small. Marauding Blight-Priest is a 3/2 that exists only for its trigger; Sanguine Syphoner attacks every turn whether or not it can be blocked. What matters is that the opponent keeps drawing: their draw step, our Gift spells, Scrawling Crawler’s upkeep trigger and Gleaming Splendor’s {2}{W} ability all feed the same three payoffs, so the deck is never short of triggers, only of cards — which is why the Splendor ability targeting us and the opponent at once is almost always correct in the mid game.
Dewdrop Cure is the engine’s reset button. With the gift promised it returns up to three creatures with mana value 2 or less, which is Razorkin Needlehead, Melancholic Poet and Sanguine Syphoner in one card. Against a wipe, that is the play that decides whether the deck still has a game.

Get Marauding Blight-Priest and Bloodthirsty Conqueror onto the board at the same time. title: Gift Economy
text:
Key interactions and edge cases







Interaction
Ruling detail




The gift resolves before the spell
A promised gift happens first, so the opponent draws (or makes the token) before the spell’s main effect. Parting Gust’s exile and Consumed by Greed’s edict still happen after the gift draw, and the draw can never take the target away because the gift is not a spell the opponent controls


Gift is optional and the word means exactly what it says
Gift a card means the opponent draws a card. Gift a tapped Fish, Gift a Food and Gift a Treasure create those tokens for them. Of the seven Gift spells in the deck only Consumed by Greed, Dewdrop Cure and Coiling Rebirth promise a card, so only those three feed Razorkin Needlehead and Scrawling Crawler


Needlehead triggers on any draw
Razorkin Needlehead does not care whose turn it is or why the card was drawn — the opponent’s own draw step counts, so the engine deals damage every turn even when the deck casts nothing


Gleaming Splendor counts draws, not turns
It triggers on the opponent’s second card drawn in a single turn. A Scrawling Crawler upkeep draw plus a promised Consumed by Greed on the same turn is exactly two, which is a Treasure. Two Splendors make two Treasures


Melancholic Poet’s repartee
It needs an instant or sorcery that targets a creature, and it triggers on the cast, not the resolution, so a Gift spell cast into a counterspell still drains 1 and gains us 1


Marauding Blight-Priest plus Bloodthirsty Conqueror
Both triggers are mandatory and neither is a may, so once one point of life is lost by an opponent the loop cannot be stopped. The loop needs both permanents in play; it does not need a Gift spell or an attack to start, and Scrawling Crawler’s upkeep trigger is enough to begin it


Nocturnal Hunger without the gift
Destroying a creature without promising the Food costs us 2 life. In races, that is sometimes correct — but the Food costs nothing and only ever gains the opponent 3 life, so promise it


Parting Gust on our own creatures
With no gift promised, the exiled creature returns at the beginning of the next end step with a +1/+1 counter, which is a way to reset a Razorkin Needlehead that has been hit by a -3/-3 effect or to re-trigger nothing at all. Its real value against our own board is protection from a sorcery-speed wipe


Coiling Rebirth’s copy
The 1/1 token copy only appears if the gift was promised and the returned creature is not legendary, which is why the deck runs no legends. Copying a Scrawling Crawler doubles the upkeep draw and both drain triggers


Restless Fortress activation timing
It is an activated ability, so it can be used after blockers are declared. The 2 life loss is the defending player’s, and the 2 life gained is ours, which is one Blight-Priest trigger whether it connects or not


Soulstone Sanctuary’s mana
It taps for colorless. Treat it as a spell land, not a source for a colored spell, and count it only when the deck has four lands and spare mana

title: Chart the Redline
text:
Overview
Three mechanics share one engine. Discover is the deck’s card advantage and its free-spell faucet: Geological Appraiser, Caparocti Sunborn, Quintorius Kand and Curator of Sun’s Creation all dig for a nonland card and cast it without paying its cost. Plan counters are the deck’s tickers: four enchantments, each counting a different event the deck already produces, and each cashing out into a burst. Start your engines! is the clock: the speed track climbs once per turn whenever an opponent loses life, and at max speed the entire board upgrades.
The joins are real, not cosmetic:

Every spell Discovered is cast from exile, so Quintorius Kand pings each opponent for 2 and gains you 2. That ping is also a life-loss event, which advances speed.
Every noncreature spell you cast (including a Discovered enchantment, a copied spell, or a Treasure-spending sorcery) adds a plan counter to Death to Our Enemies and makes a tapped Treasure, which pays for the next spell.
Every creature that enters triggers Political Triumph (scry plus counter) and Caparocti’s tap-two cost, so the token makers feed the Discover engine.
Discarding creature cards to Rewrite History and Kickoff Celebrations, and creatures dying in combat, put creature cards into the graveyard for Robot Domination, whose three counters turn into three Robot Villain tokens that attack for amplified damage.

title: Chart the Redline
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Lead with a ticker over a body when you have the choice. Political Triumph on turn one means every subsequent creature is scry plus a counter, and the fourth creature in the line turns into a team-wide +1/+1 counter plus a card. Death to Our Enemies wants you to keep casting noncreature spells, so hold it until you can follow with two or three; each one makes a tapped Treasure, which is what pays for your four-drops. Gastal Thrillseeker is the cleanest turn-two play: it deals the point of damage that puts speed on the board and it becomes a deathtouch haste attacker the moment you hit max speed.


Mid game
Geological Appraiser is the pivot. Cast it, discover 3, and cast whatever you flip. If Curator of Sun’s Creation is already down, Discover twice on the same turn: two free spells, two Quintorius triggers if the planeswalker is out, and a plan counter on Death to Our Enemies for each noncreature hit. Robot Domination is the attrition engine: every creature card that reaches your yard draws you a card and adds a counter, and the third counter turns into three 2/2 Robot Villain tokens that attack under Far Fortune’s amplifier.


The combo turn
The deck’s burst turn looks like this: Caparocti Sunborn attacks, you tap two Treasures or tokens to discover 3, Curator doubles it to a second discover 3, both spells are cast from exile, Quintorius Kand pings each opponent for 2 twice, Death to Our Enemies takes two counters and makes two tapped Treasures, and speed climbs to 4. From there Far Fortune makes every subsequent point of damage one bigger. On a developed board that is usually lethal in one attack step, and Pride of the Road gives any single attacker double strike at the beginning of combat.


Win condition two
When the board stalls, burn them out. Death to Our Enemies cashes its fourth counter for 7 damage divided among one or two targets, and Quintorius Kand converts each Discover into 2 to each opponent. Two Appraisers plus a Curator is 8 damage to each opponent from the planeswalker alone, and the Treasures those casts generate keep the chain going. The Speed Demon is the last piece of reach: flying, trample, and at end of turn it draws and drains you for your speed, which is card advantage that costs life you have usually already spent.


Mulligan guide
Keep hands with two to four lands, at least one any-color land, and one ticker or one two-drop. Starting Town plus Public Thoroughfare is a fine base. Ship hands with no red or black source, and ship hands of five lands. Do not keep a one-lander that needs a specific color on turn two.


Key interactions and edge cases

Public Thoroughfare and Command Bridge are sacrifices if you cannot tap something. Play them as lands two through four, never as land one, and remember a Treasure token is a legal tap for Public Thoroughfare.
Geological Appraiser’s Discover only triggers if you cast it. A token copy made by Slick Imitator will not discover.
Curator of Sun’s Creation triggers once each turn, so stack the biggest Discover last if you get a choice.
Discovered cards are cast, so they count as noncreature spells for Death to Our Enemies and as spells from exile for Quintorius.
Plan enchantments sacrifice themselves when the final counter is put on. Political Triumph and Death to Our Enemies are the two you most want to fire in the same turn as a lethal swing.
Soulstone Sanctuary’s animation costs four mana and does not end; activate it on the opponent’s end step when you have mana spare so it can attack with vigilance and still block.
Amonkhet Raceway’s max-speed ability gives haste, which lets a freshly cast Far Fortune attack immediately for the extra point, and lets you animate Soulstone Sanctuary and swing in the same turn.



Matchups
Against aggro, your plan tickers are slower than their clock, so trade early and let Embalmed Ascendant’s Zombie token plus Gastal Thrillseeker’s deathtouch at max speed do the blocking, then win with the amplified swing. Against control, cast your Discover creatures into open mana and keep Death to Our Enemies in hand as a threat that punishes them for tapping out; Quintorius Kand is your best card because every Discover becomes uncounterable reach. Against midrange, Robot Domination is the engine that wins the long game, and Soulstone Sanctuary plus Amonkhet Raceway let you attack from a board that looks empty.

title: Terra Ascendant
text:
Curve and mana
Sixteen cards cost two, ten cost three, six cost four and four cost five or more, on twenty-four lands with thirteen green sources, eleven white and twelve blue. The deck wants four lands by turn four and is happy to see six, because Way of the Paradox converts extra lands into loyalty and lifegain rather than flooding out.

title: Terra Ascendant
text:
Early game
Lead on a green source and a two-drop. Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes is the best turn-two play because it makes the following land drops into loyalty; Tam's Resistance is the best turn-two play when you already have an Avatar or a Way in hand, since it puts a Jace token straight to four loyalty. Do not trade Solarium Sentry or Unflinching Hortimancer for a card; they are the bodies that make the lifegain plan lethal later.

title: Terra Ascendant
section: Mid game and the combo turn
text:
Mid game and the combo turn
The combo turn is any turn that starts with Way of the Paradox on the battlefield and a Jace token at five or more loyalty:

Activate the token’s “[-3]: Draw a card” (or “[-1]: Surveil 1” when the top card is known to be bad) — this gains a life from Way of the Paradox and triggers Titanbones, Bloombrute, Kwia and Hortimancer.
Play the extra land Way of the Paradox grants — Avatar empowers Jace 2, Koth gains another life, and a Plains adds a +1/+1 counter.
Spend four loyalty on the Beast ability from Way of the Wildspeaker, or eight on the Leviathan from Kiora of Salt and Sand, and pass with a token still above zero loyalty.

Because the token only dies at zero, the sequencing rule is simple: never activate an ability that would leave the token at zero unless the body it buys is worth more than the engine. With Theorist's Sanctum untapped, two mana buys two loyalty back at instant speed if the opponent tries to attack it down.

title: Terra Ascendant
text:
Win condition 2
Titanbones, Towering Heart plus any repeatable lifegain is the deck’s honest clock: Paradox activations, Koth land drops and Solarium Sentry triggers each add two counters, so a Titanbones that survives two turns is usually a 10/9 or larger. Kiora of Salt and Sand makes it unblockable on any turn a loyalty ability was activated, and Bloombrute’s activated ability gives it trample and lifelink for the finish. Kwia Vigorbloom is the alternative: a 6/6 flying lifelink that also makes Lotus tokens, which then pay for a second spell in the same turn.

title: Terra Ascendant
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two to four lands, at least one green source, and either Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes or Way of the Paradox. A hand of Transformative Commons, Hallowed Fountain, Avatar, Tam’s Resistance is a snap keep. Ship hands with no green source, hands with only five-plus drops, and hands whose only engine is Way of the Wildspeaker without a loyalty source. Six-card hands are fine in this deck; the engine is redundant.

title: Terra Ascendant
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Way of the Paradox grants the additional land drop on the turn you activate a loyalty ability, so hold a land in hand rather than playing it out when the Way is about to land.
Empower creates the Jace token only if you do not already control one, and then puts the counters on it. Multiple empower effects in one turn stack onto the same token, which is why Tam's Resistance into a land drop can put a fresh token to six loyalty.
Countersculpt can behold the Jace token, so the two-blue counter is effectively unconditional once the engine is running.
Theorist's Sanctum can also behold the Jace token to enter untapped — behold is a choice, not a sacrifice.
Vigorbloom Charm’s fight mode is the answer to a large blocker that Kiora cannot make unblockable; the hexproof and indestructible mode protects the token from removal in response to an activation.
Kwia Vigorbloom’s Lotus token is an artifact, not a land, so it does not trigger landfall — it pays for spells instead.

title: Terra Ascendant
text:
Matchups

Aggro: the deck’s early bodies are 3/3 and 2/1, and Solarium Sentry gains 2 on every cheap opposing spell, so the first four turns are survivable. Vigorbloom Charm and Countersculpt cover the one big threat, and once Titanbones or Kwia lands the life totals swing hard.
Midrange: the best matchup. The opponent cannot out-size a board that adds loyalty on every land and counters on every life gain; save Vigorbloom Charm for their removal spell on the token.
Control: the engine sits on enchantments, lands and a planeswalker token, so sweepers only reset the creatures. Keep a land in hand to re-arm landfall immediately after a wipe, and use Way of the Cryomancer’s copy ability to double a Charm or a removal spell in the counter war.
Combo: the deck has no stack interaction beyond Countersculpt, so the plan is to race with Beasts and Leviathans and to use Kiora’s unblockable rider for exact damage. Countersculpt is for the one spell that actually ends the game.
Graveyard decks: nothing here interacts with a graveyard, so the plan is speed — a turn-four Beast plus a turn-five Titanbones is usually faster than a reanimation setup that needs its own setup turn.

Reality Fracture is Standard-legal but still carries no arena_id in the data, so the import list becomes playable on Arena once the set is enabled there.

title: Chromatic Caper
text:
Overview
Chromatic Caper fuses three build-around mechanics: Vivid (effects scale with X, the number of colors among permanents you control), Plot (pay a small cost to exile a card, then cast it later without paying its mana cost), and Alliance (creatures that trigger whenever another creature enters under your control). The deck is a five-color plot-combo engine: plot spells cheaply on turns two through four, then dump them for free in a single explosive turn. Every free creature triggers every Alliance creature, and every colored permanent you resolve pushes Vivid’s X toward the full five colors.
The engine is Fblthp, Lost on the Range, who gives the top card of your library plot and lets you plot nonland cards from the top of your library, and Make Your Own Luck, which plots a card and puts the other two into your hand. Bloom Tender is the mana core: with five colors among your permanents it taps for five mana, letting a plotted top end cast for free on the same turn you untap. Outcaster Trailblazer fixes mana on entry and draws a card whenever a 4+ power creature enters, which the free Freestrider Commandos (5/5 when cast without paying) and Slash (7/5) trigger constantly.
The kill is the fusion working at once. Slash, Reptile Rampager deals 2 damage to each opponent for every creature that enters, and creates a 2/2 Mutant token when it attacks, which enters and pings again. Meanwhile Squawkroaster grows to 5 power with five colors, and Glister Bairn hands it +5/+5 at combat, making a 10/4 double striker. Rogue’s Passage makes that creature unblockable, and Shimmercreep drains for 5 as a finisher.

Setup (turns 1-3): Play Bloom Tender, Fblthp, or Outcaster Trailblazer. Plot cards from hand or off the top (plot costs are 1-2 mana, cheaper than the cards themselves). Fix mana with Fabled Passage and Evolving Wilds.
Engine (turns 3-4): Resolve Make Your Own Luck to plot and draw. Deploy Alliance creatures: Mighty Mutanimals, Raphael, East Wind Avatar, Mutant Town Musicians. Every plot cast later turns them on.
Kill (turns 4-6): Cast plotted creatures for free in one turn. Each entry triggers every Alliance creature; Slash pings, Raphael pings, Mutanimals and East Wind grow the team. Swing; Rogue’s Passage makes Squawkroaster or Slash unblockable; Shimmercreep or Explosive Prodigy closes the last gap.

Curve and mana
Average CMC is 3.35, but the effective curve is lower because plot costs (1-2 mana) are paid early and the spells themselves are cast for free later. The deck runs 23 lands: six fetches, twelve conditional untapped duals, two utility lands (Rogue’s Passage, Restless Bivouac), and three basics. title: Chromatic Caper
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Play Bloom Tender on turn two if possible, or Fblthp on three. Use Fblthp to plot the top card of your library every turn the plot cost is payable. Outcaster Trailblazer both fixes mana and starts the draw engine. Do not rush to deploy Alliance creatures before you have plot cards banked; they are payoff pieces, not pressure.


Mid game
Bank 2-3 plotted cards with Make Your Own Luck and Fblthp. Resolve Mighty Mutanimals, Raphael, and East Wind Avatar so they are in play for the dump turn. Prismatic Undercurrents both fixes your colors and gives extra land drops, which also feeds Fabled Passage. Hold Explosive Prodigy for a blocker that would trade with Squawkroaster or Slash.


The combo turn
Cast every plotted creature for free in one turn, biggest first so Outcaster Trailblazer’s draw trigger (4+ power entries) fires. Each entry triggers all Alliance creatures: Slash deals 2 to each opponent, Raphael 1, Mutanimals puts counters, East Wind and Musicians pump. If Slash attacks, its Mutant token enters and triggers everything again. Then animate Rogue’s Passage on Squawkroaster (5/4 double strike with five colors) or Slash (7/5) and swing for the kill. Shimmercreep drains 5 life as a second finisher that also wins races.


Win condition 2: Vivid alpha strike
With five colors among permanents, Squawkroaster is a 5/4 double striker (10 damage). Glister Bairn at combat gives another creature +5/+5 until end of turn; a Bairn-buffed Squawkroaster is a 10/9 double striker (20 damage). Rogue’s Passage makes it unblockable. Explosive Prodigy clears the one blocker that matters, and East Wind Avatar’s flying chip damage adds reach over several turns.


Mulligan guide
Keep any hand with two to three lands, at least one green source and one blue or red source, and a two-drop (Bloom Tender) or an engine (Fblthp, Outcaster Trailblazer) plus a plot card. Mulligan hands with four or more lands, no early play, or only high-cost Alliance payoffs. Fblthp plus Make Your Own Luck is a strong keep.


Key interactions and edge cases

Vivid counts colors among permanents you control, including colored lands only if they are creature lands; basic and dual lands are colorless, so the fifth color comes from Shimmercreep or any other colored permanent.
Freestrider Commando gets its +1/+1 counters only if it is cast without paying mana, so always cast it from plot, never for its mana cost.
Slash’s attack token enters after combat begins; its Alliance triggers resolve before damage, so the ping can finish an opponent before blockers are declared.
Aven Interrupter exiles a spell on the stack and turns it into a plotted card; against you, that means the opponent can recast it later for free, so use it on removal aimed at Slash or Squawkroaster and accept the delayed threat.
Rogue’s Passage can be activated any time you have priority; activate it in the beginning of combat step or when declaring attackers, since the unblockable effect lasts for the whole combat.
Shimmercreep’s drain is an enters-the-battlefield trigger, so it resolves even if the creature is answered immediately.



Matchups

Aggro: Bloom Tender and early blockers (Raphael 1/3, Mutanimals token) hold the ground; Explosive Prodigy and Shimmercreep’s lifegain stabilize; the dump turn usually races faster than aggro’s clock.
Control: Fblthp’s ward 2 and Aven Interrupter’s flash answer protect the engine; Aven taxes spells cast from graveyard or exile; plot cards are uncounterable in the sense that they are cast for free later, so bank them against countermagic.
Midrange: Slash outclasses most midrange boards (7/5); the Alliance dump turn grows the team past their creatures; keep Rogue’s Passage for the turn you need to push damage through.

text:
Key interactions and edge cases







Interaction
Ruling detail




Valiant triggers once per creature per turn
Each Valiant creature has its own trigger, but only the first time that creature is targeted in a turn. Secret Tunnel’s ability targets two creatures, so it fires two different Valiant abilities with one activation - but targeting the same creature twice in a turn does nothing the second time


Equip is a targeting ability
Re-equipping Adventuring Gear each turn is a Valiant trigger on the creature that receives it. Equip only as a sorcery, so it is a main-phase trigger, not a combat trick


Earthbend lands stay lands
The awakened land is still a land, so it counts for Toph, the Blind Bandit’s power and it still taps for mana. If it dies or is exiled it returns to the battlefield tapped, so an earthbend is a permanent upgrade, not a temporary animation


Earthbend is a 0/0 base plus counters
The land enters as a 0/0 and receives counters equal to the earthbend number. Anything that removes counters or sets base power can shrink it, and a land awakened twice keeps both sets of counters


Knight of Wundagore is once per turn
Only the first counter you place on another creature each turn gives the Knight a counter. Place the biggest counter source first - Earthbend 4 or 5 rather than a one-shot Snakeskin Veil


Toph counts counters on lands, not lands
Her power is the number of +1/+1 counters on lands you control, so one land with five counters makes her a 5/3, and five lands with one counter each does the same thing


Claim the Kingdom’s indestructible counter
The fourth plan counter sacrifices the enchantment, and the indestructible counter goes on a target creature you control. Put it on the creature wearing Adventuring Gear so the pump and the protection stay together


Rockalanche counts Forests, not lands
X is the number of Forests you control, so Rockface Village, Secret Tunnel and Restless Prairie do not add to it. Flashback {5}{G} casts it a second time later, which is the last land creature of the game


Hard-Hitting Question targets your creature first
The spell is a fight effect, so the chosen creature needs to survive the exchange. It is best aimed from a boosted Seedglaive Mentor or an earthbent land creature

The deck’s clock is turn five or six, so the plan is to attack every turn and force blocks. Secret Tunnel’s unblockable activation is the way through a stalled ground, and Hard-Hitting Question answers any creature that a combo needs on the battlefield

title: Gold and Granite
text:
Curve and mana
The deck curves 8 / 13 / 5 / 8 / 2 across one through five mana (36 nonlands, average cost 2.5), and 23 of the 36 cost two or less. Counting only lands, the base gives sixteen white sources, thirteen green and thirteen red. White is the deepest because An Unexpected Party asks for {2}{W}{W}; red carries Balin, Loremaster’s {3}{R}{R} and the double strike payoffs; green exists mainly for Meltstrider’s Gear, which one green source is enough to cast. Plains plus Training Compound means the colour-conditional land is live from the moment a basic hits the board, and The Lonely Mountain is an untapped red source in any hand with an artifact.

title: Gold and Granite
text:
Early game
Turns one and two are artifacts first, legends second. Dwarven Mauler into two Equipment is a real opening: the Mauler makes its own equip abilities cost {2} less, so a turn-three Dwarven Mattock equips for {1} and a Diamond Pick-Axe equips for free. Kíli the Resourceful should be the first legend down when you have an artifact to follow, because the extra card starts immediately.
Do not hold Equipment waiting for a better carrier. Every unattached artifact still counts for Storied and still discounts The Lonely Mountain, and Kíli will draw off it. The deck wants the story online by turn three; three artifacts, legends or Sagas on the battlefield is the whole requirement.

title: Gold and Granite
text:
Mid game
Turn four is where the deck stops playing fair. Fíli the Pathfinder turns every subsequent Dwarf — including the 2/2 tokens from Dwarven Shortsword and The Lonely Mountain — into two bodies. Dáin Ironfoot then gives every equipped attacker double strike, so a 2/2 Dwarf with a Mattock (+2/+2) and a Meltstrider’s Gear (+2/+1) attacks as a 6/5 for ten damage.
An Unexpected Party is the turn that ends games: cast At the Door for X = 2 first for two 2/2 Dwarf tokens, then cast the enchantment from exile naming Dwarf so the entire company — including those tokens — is +2/+2. A board of three Dwarves and an Equipment becomes fifteen or more power on the attack, doubled by Dáin Ironfoot.

title: Gold and Granite
text:
The combo turn
The drain kill is the cleanest line in the deck. With Balin, Loremaster and Fíli the Pathfinder on the battlefield and an enduring story, cast any nontoken Dwarf. Fíli makes a 2/2 Dwarf token, Balin sees two Dwarf entries, and each trigger discards your hand, draws that many cards and deals that many damage to each opponent. A four-card hand is eight damage to each opponent from one Dwarf; a loop of Dwarven Shortsword, The Lonely Mountain tokens and Fíli’s triggers keeps the hand full while the table drains.
The swarm kill is the parallel line. Dáin Ironfoot plus two equipped attackers and Iron Hills’ two +1/+1 counters is a fourteen-to-twenty damage attack out of nowhere, and Diamond Pick-Axe’s Treasures pay for the next Equipment while the attack happens.

title: Gold and Granite
text:
Win condition 2
When the ground is stalled, the deck wins without the red zone. Balin, Loremaster converts every Dwarf entry into life loss, so Fíli’s tokens, Dwarven Shortsword tokens and The Lonely Mountain tokens are all points of damage. Because the trigger is “may discard your hand”, it can also be used purely as a free draw spell when the board is safe — discard three, draw three, no damage if the story is not yet online.

title: Gold and Granite
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep two or three lands, one cheap artifact and one Dwarf. A hand with Dwarven Mauler, Diamond Pick-Axe, Kíli the Resourceful and three lands is the ideal keep; it turns the story on by turn three and starts drawing immediately. Ship one-land hands and ship hands with no artifact at all — without three artifacts or legends the deck is a pile of small Dwarves with no anthem, no ward and no drain. A hand that is all Equipment and no creatures is also a ship unless it contains Kíli.

title: Gold and Granite
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Storied is checked once: the moment you control three artifacts, legendaries or Sagas you have an enduring story for the rest of the game, even if the board is wiped afterwards.
Kíli the Resourceful draws only once each turn, so sequence two entries into one turn only if the second one matters for combat.
Kíli’s free equip applies to the first equip ability you activate each turn, not the first Equipment you cast; equip before casting the second artifact if the discount matters.
Dáin Ironfoot’s Axe token is a real artifact — it counts for Storied, for Kíli’s trigger and for The Lonely Mountain’s discount.
Dáin Ironfoot’s attack trigger gives double strike to every equipped attacker, and it resolves before blockers, so an unblocked equipped Dwarf doubles its damage that turn.
Fíli the Pathfinder only triggers on nontoken Dwarves; the 2/2 tokens it makes do not chain further, but they do trigger Balin, Loremaster.
Balin’s trigger is optional. Never discard a hand you need to keep for a lethal attack; the draw is only worth it when the story is online or your hand is disposable.
An Unexpected Party’s adventure resolves first, so the tokens exist before the enchantment is cast from exile — the +2/+2 applies to them in the same turn.
Ragged Short Spear can be cast with an empty hand and still be a two-mana +2/+0; only discard when you have a card worth trading.
Dwarven Mattock enters attached to target Dwarf, so it is an Equipment, a Storied count and a Kíli trigger for two mana even with no creature to equip.
The Lonely Mountain enters untapped only if you already control an Equipment, so cast an artifact before playing it.
Iron Hills sacrifices itself; keep it until the turn you can attack with a pumped double-striking Dwarf, not as a colour fixer you give away early.
Training Compound makes red or green only if it entered this turn or you control a basic land, so it doubles as a colourless source for Dwarven Mattock early.
